dormitory-4-19.description: Marisol Vega's private one-person dormitory room, decorated with fashion pieces, cosmetics, gold accessories, music speakers, and carefully arranged outfits.

Campus Fresh Market.basicInfo: Campus grocery store supplying ingredients, snacks, toiletries, and daily necessities.

market-entrance.description: Entrance with specials and student discounts.

fresh-food-aisle.description: Produce, dairy, eggs, and chilled ingredients.

pantry-aisle.description: Rice, noodles, spices, drinks, and snacks.

checkout-cafe.description: Counter for coffee, sandwiches, and gossip.

Academy Walk.basicInfo: Covered arcade with clothing, gifts, electronics, school supplies, and support accessories.

uniform-shop.description: Uniforms, casual clothes, shoes, and alterations.

The Commons Table.basicInfo: Affordable restaurant where students eat, work part-time, and build relationships.

dining-room.description: Casual room with booths and group tables.

private-booths.description: Quiet booths for dates and difficult talks.

Chikara Gate Station.basicInfo: Secure campus station where enrolled students and authorized visitors can buy tickets and board trains to Tokyo districts. When the player enters, a station attendant approaches to offer route, ticket, and academy-permission help.

concourse.description: Academy transit hall with route boards, student access checks, ticket machines, and staff assistance. You can buy a train ticket here before boarding.

ticket-counter.description: Campus ticket counter and student transit desk. The game should tell the player they can buy a ticket here, choose a destination, and pay the listed fare; school-hour permission may still be required.

platforms.description: Platforms for Academy District and approved connections through Central Tokyo. Boarding requires a valid ticket and any required academy authorization.

Hero Field Complex.basicInfo: Outdoor training zone for rescue drills, mobility practice, controlled sparring, and team exercises.

field-complex.description: Training fields with adjustable terrain and safety barriers.

rescue-village.description: Mock neighborhood for evacuation and disaster-response drills.

mobility-track.description: Walls, ramps, platforms, and timed traversal routes.

flood-course.description: Water-and-current course for aquatic rescue practice.

observation-tower.description: Instructor tower for reviewing team tactics.

Pixel Riot Arcade.basicInfo: Arcade hiring students for cabinet maintenance assistance, prize counter service, floor monitoring, and evening customer support.

front-desk.description: Entry desk handling tokens, memberships, questions, and customer issues.

game-floor.description: Arcade floor needing monitoring, cleanup, and basic player assistance.

prize-counter.description: Prize exchange and inventory station for tickets and merchandise.

staff-room.description: Small staff area for breaks, schedules, and shift instructions.

Gearshift Support Shop.basicInfo: Support-equipment retailer offering part-time work in customer service, inventory, repairs, demonstrations, and hero gear organization.

showroom.description: Display floor for approved support items, costumes, tools, and training accessories.

repair-counter.description: Work area for intake, basic maintenance, testing, and customer requests.

inventory-room.description: Storage area for stock, deliveries, labels, and equipment records.

WorkLink Exchange.basicInfo: Central job board connecting students and residents with legal part-time shifts, pay details, schedules, and employer instructions.

job-board.description: Notice wall and digital board listing shifts, pay, hours, and requirements.

Obsidian Crown Agency Headquarters.basicInfo: A fortified supervillain agency headquarters occupying a sealed forty-eight-story skyscraper above an abandoned financial district. The agency presents itself as a legitimate security consultancy while coordinating criminal contracts, covert weapons, protected metahuman operations, mercenary deployments, and assassination work. Most floors are offices, storage, residences, laboratories, security infrastructure, or restricted operational space.

street-approach.description: Rain-slick perimeter streets beneath the tower. Patrols, snipers, armored response vans, powered scouts, cameras, and civilians trapped behind a security cordon create the first encounter.

public-lobby.description: A polished reception hall hiding criminal operations behind a legal front. Guards, shielded enforcers, combat drones, a disguised powered bodyguard, frightened staff, and a staged hostage scene confront intruders.

ground-elevators.description: A bank of reinforced elevators and biometric access gates connecting the lobby to the tower's forty-eight floors. Security staff can lock individual cars, redirect them, or trap passengers between checkpoints.

loading-bay.description: An underground cargo entrance for contraband, power-enhancing drugs, weapons, prisoners, armored vehicles, and mercenary teams. An armored convoy, explosive haulers, drug-enhanced bruisers, drone swarms, and a security lieutenant defend it.

warehouse-floor.description: A concealed storage level with drug shipments, restraints, evidence lockers, unstable powered test subjects, containment beasts, turret nests, coerced workers, and an elite warehouse commander.

containment-lab.description: A hidden laboratory where the agency tests suppressants and amplifiers on captured powered people. Researchers, automated defenses, unstable subjects, and a power-suppressing specialist create a rescue-or-pursuit encounter.

security-control.description: The surveillance and communications hub controlling cameras, doors, elevators, alarms, drones, and turrets. Tactical operators, a lockdown team, a handler with armed escorts, and falsified mission records defend it.

evidence-office.description: A records room containing contracts, political protection payments, target intelligence, assassination dossiers, and proof that official reports were altered. An archivist, security detail, and timed data purge force an investigation under pressure.

operations-floor.description: A fortified mid-tower operations level where criminal contracts are assigned, mercenary teams are briefed, powered assets are tracked, and extraction routes are coordinated. The floor can become a command center, an ambush site, or a contested objective.

executive-floor.description: A restricted upper floor protected by powered lieutenants, invisible hunters, regeneration specialists, armored bodyguards, and an emergency response team. Rival agents, assassination clients, and captured witnesses may alter the route to the target.

rooftop.description: The exposed roof of the forty-eight-story skyscraper: rain-dark concrete, antenna masts, maintenance structures, helipad markings, service access, and a panoramic view over the abandoned financial district. It is a lonely insertion and extraction point, covered by floodlights, cameras, sniper nests, powered sentries, and rapid-response routes from the upper floors. A contractor may sit here alone before an operation while Ichi speaks through an ordinary Bluetooth earbud; once the alarm begins, the roof becomes a lethal kill zone.

target-suite.description: A hardened private suite containing a protected supervillain target, personal superpowered guards, defensive constructs, and possible reinforcements. A contract may demand assassination, but the encounter must allow killing, restraint, capture, rescue, negotiation, or abandoning the objective. One Blacklisted member faces the mission's fatal turning point here or during the approach.

Tokyo Curse Squad Headquarters.basicInfo: A concealed headquarters beneath a restored shrine compound in Old Tokyo. The Tokyo Curse Squad gathers here to shelter cursed-item wielders, magical practitioners, and supernatural power users; negotiate with spirits; research dangerous artifacts; and protect the surrounding neighborhood.
Tokyo Curse Squad Headquarters.hiddenInfo: The headquarters predates modern hero licensing. Beneath the archive is an older sealed chamber whose pact may protect Old Tokyo—or bind the entire Tokyo Curse Squad to an unknown supernatural power.

shrine-courtyard.description: A quiet restored shrine courtyard with protective ropes, paper charms, and a sealed entrance beneath the main altar. Locals visit without knowing the headquarters lies below.

reception-hall.description: A hidden meeting hall where new members, heroes, spirits, and neighborhood elders negotiate access, protection, and supernatural disputes.

archive-vault.description: A warded archive containing cursed objects, magical texts, family records, spirit contracts, and containment cases. Every item is catalogued because careless handling can awaken it.

ritual-chamber.description: A circular chamber for spellwork, pact renewal, exorcism, magical training, and controlled experiments. Protective seals fail if a practitioner ignores the agreed limits.

containment-ward.description: A reinforced medical and holding area for cursed artifacts, possessed objects, injured supernatural members, and entities that cannot safely return to the streets.

training-yard.description: An enclosed underground courtyard for practicing supernatural abilities, cursed-item control, close combat, and nonlethal restraint without exposing Old Tokyo.

tea-room.description: A calm traditional room used for meals, confidential conversations, mediation, and negotiations with Kurokawa contacts or skeptical hero officials.

mission-room.description: A map room displaying Old Tokyo wards, spirit routes, artifact sightings, missing-person reports, and requests for discreet supernatural assistance. Members receive rescue, containment, investigation, negotiation, and escort assignments here.

Pulse Afterdark.basicInfo: A stylish all-ages-by-time nightlife venue in Central Tokyo with music, dancing, performances, private booths, and a late-night café. Its programming changes by hour, allowing ordinary social scenes alongside celebrity events, Spark dates, and discreet meetings.
Pulse Afterdark.hiddenInfo: The club's owner quietly bans predatory behavior and cooperates with trusted staff, medics, and security contacts when a guest is in danger. A locked service room contains old event ledgers that may connect performers, heroes, villains, and supernatural visitors.

entrance-lobby.description: Neon-lit entrance with coat check, ticketing, event checks, and a visible code of conduct.

main-floor.description: Dance floor and stage for DJs, live music, hero-themed performances, student showcases, and crowded social encounters.

private-booths.description: Reserved seating for dates, group conversations, negotiations, and quieter scenes away from the music.

backstage.description: Performer preparation area and service corridor where artists, staff, guests, and suspicious activity may intersect.

late-night-cafe.description: A calmer café section serving food and non-alcoholic drinks, suitable for conversations, recovery, Spark dates, and unexpected meetings.

The Hero's Afterparty.basicInfo: A supervised campus-adjacent nightlife venue for adult Chikara Academy students and approved guests, with music, dancing, performances, karaoke, Spark dates, and late-night social scenes.
The Hero's Afterparty.hiddenInfo: The venue is independent from the academy but maintains a conduct agreement with campus staff. Security quietly contacts faculty, medics, or trusted heroes when a guest is in danger. Its event book contains connections between students, performers, agencies, villains, and supernatural visitors.

entrance-lobby.description: Secure entrance with event check-in, coat storage, accessibility support, and a visible consent and power-safety code.

nightclub-floor.description: Dance floor with student DJs, themed nights, safe lighting, and carefully monitored power effects.

student-lounge.description: Quiet seating and café area for conversation, group gatherings, Spark dates, and cooling down after performances.

performance-stage.description: Small stage for student bands, hero-brand showcases, karaoke, club fundraisers, and comedy nights.

Nightshade Exchange Relay.basicInfo: A discreet Tokyo contact point for the global Nightshade Exchange. New operators can begin through the Nightshade app without visiting in person, while the relay handles identity checks, equipment, payments, emergency extraction, and higher-risk contracts, including optional assassination listings.
Nightshade Exchange Relay.hiddenInfo: The Nightshade app is the easiest entry point for new players. It offers an onboarding profile, beginner contracts, payment previews, risk labels, anonymous messaging, and optional in-person relay access. The app never guarantees safety or legality. Contracts may involve ordinary crime, villain operations, assassination, coercion, rescue, information, or betrayal. Assassination listings must identify the requested outcome and known civilian risk, but target identity, client motives, and evidence may be unreliable. Players can investigate, refuse, negotiate, choose surveillance or extraction instead, expose the client, betray the broker, or leave the network. Distinguish suspects and jobs by evidence rather than assuming every contact is a supervillain.

front-room.description: A plausible private office and waiting room where visitors verify an invitation, identity, or referral before receiving contract information.

contract-room.description: A secured room with encrypted terminals, paper files, payment terms, and rotating job listings from Nightshade Exchange cells around the world. Some listings involve assassination, while others offer surveillance, sabotage, extraction, protection, or information work.

exit-alley.description: A narrow service alley used for discreet arrivals, departures, dead drops, and emergency exits.

Chikara Community Gym.basicInfo: An affordable neighborhood gym with free weights, cardio equipment, mats, lockers, and open floor space for general conditioning and supervised martial-arts practice.
Chikara Community Gym.hiddenInfo: Characters can train Close Quarters Combat here through regular practice, partner drills, conditioning, and instruction. Progress requires time and effort; the gym does not grant instant skill levels or assume a character has a trainer.

main-floor.description: A busy training floor with machines, weights, mats, and enough open space for footwork and conditioning drills.

mat-room.description: A padded room for stretching, grappling drills, mobility work, and controlled partner practice.

locker-room.description: Lockers, showers, water stations, and a small first-aid cabinet.

Redline Boxing Club.basicInfo: A serious boxing gym known for disciplined coaching, heavy bags, technical drills, controlled sparring, and amateur bouts.
Redline Boxing Club.hiddenInfo: Redline specializes in boxing fundamentals and controlled sparring. Characters can build Close Quarters Combat through lessons, drills, and consensual practice, with injury and recovery handled realistically.

ring-floor.description: A boxing ring surrounded by heavy bags, speed bags, mirrors, and coaches correcting stance, guard, timing, and combinations.

conditioning-corner.description: Jump ropes, medicine balls, pads, and equipment for footwork, endurance, and striking drills.

reception.description: A small front desk with membership information, class schedules, and notices for supervised bouts.

Harborline Boxing Academy.basicInfo: A waterfront boxing school that combines traditional boxing instruction with practical self-defense, fitness classes, and community outreach.
Harborline Boxing Academy.hiddenInfo: This academy can support both Close Quarters Combat training and character development through mentorship, discipline, and community relationships. It does not automatically grant formal credentials or assume the character joins a faction.

training-hall.description: A bright hall with two rings, padded walls, heavy bags, and coaches teaching boxing, defense, distance, and controlled takedown transitions.

classroom.description: A small room for rules, fight analysis, strategy, and lessons on safe, lawful self-defense.

recovery-room.description: A supervised space for hydration, stretching, ice, first aid, and post-training assessment.

entrance.description: A waterfront entrance with class boards, community notices, and a view toward the harbor.

Oblivion's Crucible Training Ring.basicInfo: A reinforced private training ring attached to Oblivion's Crucible, offering brutal practice, sparring, and combat coaching for operators willing to accept dangerous terms.
Oblivion's Crucible Training Ring.hiddenInfo: Training here can improve Close Quarters Combat through high-risk sparring and specialized coaching, but injuries, debts, reputation changes, recruitment pressure, and exposure to criminal networks are possible. Do not force a character to accept terms or participate in lethal fights.

training-ring.description: A reinforced ring with hard lighting, battered pads, observation balconies, and equipment chosen for punishing close-range drills.

equipment-bay.description: Protective gear, wraps, training weapons, and recovery supplies available under the Crucible's rules.

observer-gallery.description: A shadowed gallery where recruiters, gamblers, instructors, and rivals watch training sessions.

Deadbeats Club.basicInfo: A shared four-bedroom house in Tokyo designed as an open sandbox hub for solo or multiplayer characters. For the Deadbeat Club story start, this is the player's current home and residence: phrases such as "go home" resolve here unless the player explicitly changes residence. The house supports cooperative scenes, private downtime, planning, conflict, guests, and departures into the wider city.
Deadbeats Club.hiddenInfo: The Deadbeats Club is a neutral sandbox hub for solo or multiplayer play, not an automatic academy, faction, or romance route. For the Deadbeat Club story start, treat Deadbeats Club as the player's current residence and resolve "go home" here unless the player explicitly establishes another home. A solo player may occupy one bedroom and manage the house independently; a group may use up to four bedroom slots. Privacy, access, guests, chores, shared expenses, house rules, relationships, ownership, jobs, powers, and obligations remain player-directed. Keep legal hero work, ordinary employment, criminal offers, and other survival paths open-ended.

common-room.description: The shared living room and kitchen form the social center of the house, with a dining table, couches, storage, and doors leading toward every bedroom. Players can plan together, cook, host guests, argue, relax, or leave for the city.

bedroom-1.description: A private bedroom reserved for a player or resident chosen by the group. Its furniture, decorations, locks, and privacy rules are player-directed.

bedroom-2.description: A private bedroom reserved for a player or resident chosen by the group. Its furniture, decorations, locks, and privacy rules are player-directed.

bedroom-3.description: A private bedroom reserved for a player or resident chosen by the group. Its furniture, decorations, locks, and privacy rules are player-directed.

bedroom-4.description: A private bedroom reserved for a player or resident chosen by the group. Its furniture, decorations, locks, and privacy rules are player-directed.

bathroom.description: A shared bathroom with a shower, sink, medicine cabinet, and limited privacy. Residents decide schedules, supplies, and boundaries.

balcony.description: A narrow balcony overlooking Tokyo rooftops, useful for fresh air, private conversations, watching the street, or noticing unusual activity.

front-step.description: The house's visible front step and small entry landing, where residents wait for rides, receive deliveries, meet guests, or talk under the streetlight.

side-alley.description: A publicly visible side alley beside the house, with bins, utility pipes, and a view toward the neighborhood street. Useful for deliveries, tense conversations, and optional encounters.

laundry-corner.description: A cramped laundry and utility corner off the common room, with cleaning supplies, a washer, and household notices. Ordinary chores and low-stakes conversations happen here.

fire-escape.description: A visible fire escape reached from the balcony, overlooking neighboring rooftops. Suitable for late-night conversations and quiet observation, subject to safety and weather.

rooftop-access.description: A shared rooftop access landing above the house, with a broad city view and enough space to sit away from the street. Visible and reachable, though building rules and weather may restrict use.

MealDrop Fulfillment Hub.basicInfo: A busy urban grocery and prepared-food dispatch center serving the MealDrop app, with shelves for essentials, restaurant pickup lanes, courier staging, and refrigerated storage.
MealDrop Fulfillment Hub.hiddenInfo: MealDrop is primarily an ordinary service location and is not automatically a quest hub. Characters may work here, collect orders, solve delivery problems, or encounter ordinary NPCs. Do not turn routine food delivery into a crisis unless player choices or current world events support it.

dispatch-floor.description: Workers assemble grocery baskets and prepared-food orders beside route screens, packing stations, and insulated delivery bags.

courier-bay.description: A loading area where bicycle, scooter, and walking couriers collect orders for nearby deliveries.

cold-storage.description: Refrigerated and frozen storage for groceries, drinks, medical-safe foods, and restaurant ingredients.

Tokyo Financial District Exchange.basicInfo: A regulated financial services center with bank branches, brokerage offices, card support desks, payment services, and public investment education.
Tokyo Financial District Exchange.hiddenInfo: This is an ordinary financial-services location, not a guaranteed source of money. Account approval, loans, credit, trading access, and investment outcomes depend on established identity, funds, legal status, records, and player decisions. Financial crime, fraud, market manipulation, and stolen credentials create legal and faction consequences.

banking-hall.description: A public banking hall for account services, transfers, card support, identity checks, and payment questions.

brokerage-lounge.description: A supervised space for market information, brokerage support, investment education, and lawful trading assistance.

service-entrance.description: A side entrance used by staff, couriers, and scheduled appointments.

Chikara Academy Campus Faculty Housing.basicInfo: Private one-bedroom faculty apartments on the Chikara Academy campus, with shared kitchens, common rooms, staff facilities, and quiet residential corridors for teachers and authorized faculty. Handler and Grant “Afterimage” Mercer live here in assigned private faculty apartments.
Chikara Academy Campus Faculty Housing.hiddenInfo: Handler and Grant have separate private apartments. Shared spaces make casual faculty relationships possible, while private apartments preserve boundaries and personal downtime. Grant's professional scandal, depression, and alcohol dependence may affect his availability, but faculty housing is not a clinic, bar, or criminal headquarters.

faculty-apartment-1-bedroom.description: A private one-bedroom apartment assigned to a faculty member, with a bedroom, bathroom, compact living space, desk, and kitchenette. It is the player's starting home for the new academic year and one of the faculty residences used by Grant when he is off duty.

faculty-common-room.description: A comfortable shared lounge for faculty residents, with seating, noticeboards, campus schedules, and a place for informal introductions and staff conversations.

shared-kitchen.description: A communal faculty kitchen with refrigerators, counters, tea supplies, simple cooking equipment, and a dining table used by staff residents at irregular hours.

faculty-corridor.description: A quiet residential corridor connecting private faculty apartments to the shared common room and kitchen. Staff may pass through between campus duties without being forced into social scenes.

Misfit Hero Agency Headquarters.basicInfo: A licensed but black-sheep hero agency on Hero Agency Row, assigned daily missions despite its poor reputation. The agency is underfunded, overworked, and full of improvised repairs, but the newly graduated player and three dysfunctional teammates gradually turn it into a found-family home base. The player's private apartment occupies the floor directly above the agency, while Azrael, Luna, and Tess each have their own private apartment in the same converted building.
Misfit Hero Agency Headquarters.hiddenInfo: The agency's poor reputation is partly inherited from failed leadership, but its case records contain evidence that the team was repeatedly given impossible assignments. The headquarters receives daily work because senior agencies use it as a pressure valve for politically awkward, low-prestige, or high-risk cases. The converted building's private apartments allow Azrael, Luna, Tess, and the player to live near one another without erasing privacy or consent. Shared meals, drinking nights, arguments, and unexpected support gradually create found-family bonds.

reception-dispatch.description: A cramped reception and dispatch area with ringing phones, case folders, public complaints, client requests, and a mission board that receives new assignments every day. The team must report for daily dispatch even when the job is embarrassing, dangerous, or politically inconvenient.

team-lounge.description: The agency's shared lounge with mismatched couches, a small dining table, vending machines, personal clutter, and the unofficial emotional center of the team. Arguments, meals, apologies, and found-family bonding happen here between daily missions.

shared-kitchen.description: A compact communal kitchen stocked with cheap groceries, instant meals, mismatched mugs, and notes about whose turn it is to clean. It is available for casual team scenes and practical household routines before and after daily assignments.

briefing-room.description: A glass-walled briefing room with city maps, case screens, agency regulations, and a whiteboard covered in half-erased plans. Daily mission briefings, strategy, performance reviews, and arguments over agency orders happen here.

training-room.description: A reinforced but imperfect training room with padded flooring, repair patches, target equipment, and a damage report clipboard. The team drills, argues about technique, and learns to cover one another's weaknesses between daily missions.

equipment-bay.description: A cluttered equipment bay for costumes, support gear, spare parts, transport maintenance, and emergency repairs. Gear disputes and improvised upgrades are common after the team's daily assignments.

med-bay.description: A modest agency first-aid room for stabilization, injury checks, recovery planning, and deciding when a case requires Professional Hero Hospital. Daily missions may end here without forcing the player back into action before recovery.

director-office.description: A small office for the agency director, evaluations, licensing paperwork, budget warnings, disciplinary conversations, and difficult decisions about the team's future. The director assigns or relays daily missions and manages the agency's black-sheep status.

player-apartment.description: A private apartment directly above the agency headquarters, assigned to the newly graduated player. It has a bedroom, bathroom, small living area, work desk, storage for hero equipment, and enough separation to decompress while remaining close enough to respond to daily dispatches.

azrael-apartment.description: Azrael's private apartment in the converted building above and behind the agency offices. It includes a cramped living space, a work desk covered in licensing paperwork, controlled smoking areas, and private space for the demon owner to recover after managing the team.

luna-apartment.description: Luna's private apartment in the converted agency building. Its safety plan, grounding objects, locked equipment storage, quiet space, and carefully managed access support her autonomy while reducing risk during severe power instability. Entry remains privacy- and consent-based except for genuine emergencies.

tess-apartment.description: Tess's private apartment in the converted agency building. It has practical storage, recovery space, spare blankets, meal supplies, and room for her to step away from caretaking duties when she needs support herself.

agency-street.description: The agency's entrance on Hero Agency Row, with public foot traffic, reporters, neighboring agencies, delivery workers, and occasional clients or protesters. The black-sheep agency remains licensed, but its reputation makes every daily arrival visible.

Apartment 68.basicInfo: A modest rented apartment assigned to the player near the police district. It is private, ordinary, and practical: a bedroom, small living area, kitchenette, bathroom, secure storage for duty equipment, and a place to decompress after patrols and investigations.
Apartment 68.hiddenInfo: Apartment 68 is close enough to the police district for practical commuting but is not automatically a police safehouse. It is visible and available only within the On the Beat playthrough, not a general-world location for unrelated story starts. The player controls who enters and what personal routines happen here, subject to ordinary law and building rules.

apartment-interior.description: The main private living space, with a small sofa, work surface, kitchenette, dining counter, ordinary storage, and room for quiet conversations or decompression after a shift.

bedroom.description: A private bedroom with a bed, wardrobe, bedside table, and enough quiet for sleep, recovery, and personal routines between police shifts.

kitchenette.description: A compact kitchenette with a refrigerator, microwave, sink, limited counter space, and basic cooking supplies. It supports ordinary meals rather than professional food preparation.

bathroom.description: A private bathroom with a shower, sink, mirror, and medicine cabinet for ordinary hygiene and recovery routines.

duty-storage.description: A lockable storage closet for legally issued duty equipment, uniforms, case materials, and secured personal items. It is not a police evidence locker and should not store unauthorized evidence.

apartment-entry.description: The apartment entrance and short shared hallway, with a lockable front door, mail slot, utility panel, and access toward the building stairwell. Neighbors may be heard nearby, but entry remains private and consent-based.

window-seat.description: A narrow window seat overlooking the police district, useful for reviewing notes, decompressing after patrol, watching rain, or having a quiet late-night conversation.

building-stairwell.description: The visible shared stairwell outside Apartment 68, connecting the apartment floor to the building entrance. It supports neighbor encounters, deliveries, and brief conversations.

building-entry.description: The building's public entrance and mail area, with intercoms, notices, parcel shelves, and a view of the street. A practical starting point for patrols and visitors.

street-side-alley.description: A visible side alley beside the apartment building, lit by security lamps and used by residents, deliveries, and pedestrians. Suitable for discreet but not hidden conversations.

Spaceship Crash Site.basicInfo: A concealed crash site in Chikara Tokyo where an extraterrestrial craft came down beyond the main roads. Twisted hull fragments, scorched earth, strange light patterns, and damaged alien systems mark the impact. The site is globally accessible but may draw police, heroes, scavengers, scientists, criminals, or curious civilians depending on who learns about it.
Spaceship Crash Site.hiddenInfo: Zee is the surviving space princess associated with the crashed craft. Her exact species, homeworld, powers, political enemies, and reasons for coming to Earth remain undefined until established through play or creator decisions. The crash site is not automatically safe, public, or controlled by any faction. Do not reveal Zee's origin or royal status as fact before the story supports it.

impact-crater.description: The central impact crater, scattered with wreckage, scorched ground, unstable power cells, and a damaged starship hull. Approach is physically hazardous and evidence may be disturbed by heat, gravity shifts, or residual energy.

hull-breach.description: A torn opening in the alien craft leading into dim corridors filled with unfamiliar consoles, emergency lights, sealed compartments, and signs that someone survived the crash.

command-cabin.description: The damaged command cabin with navigation displays, star charts, security locks, and fragmented records that may identify Zee's origin or pursuers.

medical-bay.description: An alien medical bay containing damaged treatment equipment, specimen restraints, emergency supplies, and clues about Zee's injuries or biology. Access may require consent, translation, or careful technical work.

perimeter.description: The edge of the crash site, where tire tracks, emergency markers, scavenger paths, and possible surveillance reveal who has discovered the impact. It is the safest place to observe before entering.

Kurokawa District.basicInfo: A dense backstreet district of aging apartments, shuttered businesses, service alleys, rooftop routes, and overlooked residents. The area is a natural operating ground for vigilantes, gangs, couriers, and anyone trying to stay outside the official spotlight.
Kurokawa District.hiddenInfo: Several buildings have unofficial rooftop access routes known to local couriers and vigilantes. The safest paths depend on weather, lighting, patrols, and which residents are awake.

backstreet-crossroads.description: A cramped intersection beneath tangled utility lines, lined with convenience stores, worn apartment entrances, and narrow alleys that make surveillance difficult.

rooftop-access.description: A fire-escape landing and locked stairwell provide access to connected rooftops. From here, a watcher can observe several blocks without standing in the street.

rooftop-route.description: A broken but traversable chain of rooftops, water tanks, maintenance bridges, and laundry lines. It is useful for couriers and surveillance but dangerous in bad weather or a hurried pursuit.

service-alley.description: A narrow rear lane behind restaurants, workshops, and abandoned units. Deliveries, discarded equipment, gang lookouts, and quiet meetings sometimes pass through here.

ramen-row.description: A short stretch of late-night ramen shops, vending machines, and covered stools. It is one of the few places where residents, couriers, vigilantes, and exhausted workers can share space without asking too many questions.

night-bars.description: A row of cramped bars, karaoke rooms, and half-hidden entrances beneath apartment buildings. Information moves quickly here, but so do rumors, debts, and unwanted attention.

gang-hideout.description: An abandoned neighborhood storefront with a reinforced rear room and access to a maintenance roof. Its occupants change, but gang crews use it for meetings, storage, intimidation, and holding people who cannot safely go to the police.

apartment-block.description: A worn residential building overlooking the district. Residents share thin walls, unreliable elevators, and a constant awareness of who controls the street below. Fire escapes and maintenance stairs create routes between the street and roof.

Central Tokyo.basicInfo: A dense central district of business towers, transit corridors, polished public spaces, nightlife, rooftops, and hidden service routes. Official heroes, media, executives, students, criminals, and ordinary workers overlap here, making it useful for investigations, social scenes, emergencies, and high-visibility missions.
Central Tokyo.hiddenInfo: Corporate security, media crews, and official heroes monitor the central district closely. Rooftops and service levels provide alternate routes, but access rules and cameras change frequently.

station-concourse.description: A crowded transit concourse where commuters, couriers, tourists, and suspicious watchers pass beneath electronic signs and constant announcements.

business-avenue.description: A canyon of office towers, convenience stores, cafés, banks, and corporate entrances. Security cameras and polished sidewalks conceal service doors and private conflicts.

rooftop-gardens.description: Elevated gardens and accessible tower roofs offering views across Central Tokyo. Some are public retreats; others are restricted maintenance spaces used for surveillance or clandestine meetings.

media-plaza.description: A bright public square surrounded by screens, broadcast studios, hero advertising, cafés, and event stages. A small incident here can become citywide news within minutes.

arcade-quarter.description: A lively strip of arcades, karaoke rooms, casual restaurants, and late-night shops beneath the central towers. It is a social hub and a useful place to follow rumors without looking like an investigator.

taxi-stand.description: A busy curbside pickup zone where taxis, rideshares, delivery vehicles, and private cars compete for space. Drivers and dispatchers notice who is moving through the city and when.

service-level.description: A maze of loading bays, utility corridors, parking access, and staff-only doors beneath the polished central district. It is useful for covert movement but easy to become disoriented in.

Old Tokyo.basicInfo: A historic district of shrine roads, lantern streets, traditional shops, theaters, tea houses, aging apartments, and preserved buildings surrounded by modern Tokyo. It is a strong setting for cultural events, secrets, personal histories, quiet investigations, and conflicts hidden behind tradition.
Old Tokyo.hiddenInfo: Old Tokyo's strongest information network is social memory: shopkeepers, caretakers, performers, and residents notice disruptions long before official systems do.

lantern-quarter.description: A narrow historic street of lanterns, small restaurants, craft shops, and old façades. Crowds gather during festivals, while residents know which doors are welcoming and which are not.

shrine-road.description: A winding approach lined with gates, stone walls, small shrines, and quiet side paths. Visitors come for blessings, rumors, memorials, and private conversations away from the main streets.

tea-market.description: A covered market of tea merchants, sweets, antique goods, and family-run stalls. Bargaining, gossip, and long-standing obligations shape who receives help here.

theater-row.description: A cluster of historic theaters, rehearsal halls, dressing rooms, and small performance venues. Public culture and private rivalries share the same narrow corridors.

heritage-gardens.description: A preserved garden and museum edge with ponds, footbridges, stone lanterns, and secluded corners. It offers calm routes, ceremonial gatherings, and places where someone can disappear into a crowd.

old-apartments.description: Aging residences above workshops and family businesses. Tenants rely on personal trust, informal favors, and neighbors who remember events the official records forgot.

old-station.description: A historic station preserved beside modern transit infrastructure. Its platforms, pedestrian bridges, and storage corridors connect the district to the rest of Tokyo.

Tokyo Bay.basicInfo: A broad waterfront district of piers, marinas, logistics yards, aquarium attractions, promenades, storm barriers, and industrial back channels. It supports rescue missions, smuggling investigations, faction operations, quiet meetings, and dangerous weather-driven events.
Tokyo Bay.hiddenInfo: The bay's public spaces and industrial routes operate on different schedules. Weather, tides, port shifts, security closures, and ferry service can change available paths and mission difficulty.

waterfront-promenade.description: A public walkway beside the bay with food stalls, benches, observation points, and sudden views of ships, bridges, and storm fronts.

ferry-pier.description: A working passenger pier shared by commuters, tourists, service crews, and small cargo operators. Departures, delays, and tide conditions shape movement through the waterfront.

aquarium-front.description: A family-oriented aquarium and attraction district that becomes quieter after closing. Service entrances, staff corridors, and waterfront access create opportunities for rescue or infiltration scenes.

logistics-yards.description: A maze of containers, cranes, warehouses, loading lanes, and restricted gates. Shipments can be legitimate, stolen, or deliberately misdeclared, and visibility changes with weather and shift changes.

warehouse-row.description: A line of old warehouses and converted storage buildings along the industrial edge. Some are legitimate businesses; others are temporary bases, smuggling points, or places where people are held.

marina.description: A mixed-use marina with private boats, repair slips, floating walkways, and small waterfront restaurants. Boat owners, mechanics, and dock workers form an informal information network.

storm-barrier.description: A long flood-control structure with maintenance stairs and restricted service platforms. It is a dramatic lookout but becomes hazardous during high winds, heavy rain, or emergency closures.

Academy District Hub.basicInfo: A lively student-centered point of interest near the academy district, combining public gathering spaces, transit access, food, study areas, shops, residences, and useful mission routes.
Academy District Hub.hiddenInfo: The public hub's lanes, residences, and clinic create privacy, rescue, investigation, and pursuit opportunities. It remains a shared space, not a faction headquarters.

district-plaza.description: A broad public plaza with benches, vending machines, event posters, and open space for gatherings, protests, performances, and emergencies.

station-entrance.description: A busy station entrance used by students, commuters, delivery workers, and visitors throughout the day.

student-quarter.description: Affordable apartments, shared houses, laundromats, and study cafés full of friendships, rumors, homesickness, and private conflicts.

food-stalls.description: A covered strip of ramen, curry, crepes, and inexpensive meals where students, workers, and residents gather.

shopping-walk.description: A pedestrian street with bookstores, uniform shops, support-item services, cafés, and practical stores.

student-café.description: A quiet café and study space for work, conversations, waiting, and shelter during bad weather.

service-lane.description: A delivery and maintenance lane behind the public areas, linking loading doors, utilities, and poorly lit shortcuts.

back-lane.description: A cramped lane behind food stalls and shops with fire escapes, locked doors, recycling cages, and useful sightlines for witnesses, discreet following, or escape.

community-clinic.description: A small walk-in clinic for students, workers, and residents. Staff may notice patterns of injuries, exhaustion, or repeated visitors.

The Quiet Ledger.basicInfo: A run-down hotel used as the Backstreet Vigilantes' discreet headquarters. Its boarded windows, unreliable elevators, empty rooms, rooftop access, and half-functioning utilities make it look abandoned enough to avoid casual attention while still providing shelter, planning space, and emergency treatment. Ken Kuroda, Maya Ishikawa, and Akari Tenno are the three core faction members living here, each with a private room; member-room-c is reserved as an offered private room for a recruited player.
The Quiet Ledger.hiddenInfo: The hotel appears vacant because ownership records are tangled and the building's public utilities are inconsistent. Ken Kuroda and Maya Ishikawa live in member-room-a and member-room-b, while Akari Tenno has her own private room elsewhere in the headquarters; member-room-c is reserved for a recruited player. Schedules, injuries, missions, loneliness, privacy, and personal boundaries determine who is actually present or available. The faction maintains fallback rooms and avoids making the headquarters indispensable to any single member.

hotel-lobby.description: A dusty lobby with a dead front desk bell, faded travel posters, and a security camera that works only when someone remembers to repair it. Visitors are screened here before being allowed farther inside.

stairwell.description: A narrow concrete stairwell connecting the lobby, room floors, and roof. The elevator is unreliable, so members use the stairs when they need quiet movement or a fast escape.

room-floor.description: A hallway of abandoned guest rooms, patched doors, mattresses, storage crates, and three occupied member rooms. The residents keep different schedules and boundaries, so a closed door generally means privacy is expected.

common-room.description: A former guest lounge with mismatched chairs, a battered television, board games, charging cables, and a noticeboard. It is the most likely place to find members between patrols, though nobody is required to socialize.

kitchen.description: A narrow communal kitchen with a repaired refrigerator, cheap cookware, labeled shelves, and food bought by whoever had time to shop. Meals are one of the few reliable chances for the residents to check in with one another.

dispatcher-room.description: A former guest room converted into a communications room for the faction dispatcher. Radios, phones, charging stations, district maps, and message logs are kept here; calls are limited to plausible missions and established contacts.

member-room-a.description: A private room occupied by one of the three current Backstreet Vigilantes. It contains personal gear, clothes, recovery supplies, and reminders of a life that existed before the faction. Entering without permission is a serious breach of trust.

member-room-b.description: A private room occupied by one of the three current Backstreet Vigilantes. Its occupant keeps their own routine, equipment, and boundaries, and may be asleep, away, injured, or unwilling to talk.

member-room-c.description: A private room reserved for a recruited player at the Backstreet Vigilantes' headquarters. It is offered only after the interview and acceptance of the group's secrecy rules; until then, it remains an empty, prepared room rather than an assumed residence.

planning-room.description: A former conference room converted into a planning space with district maps, radios, charging cables, case files, and multiple ways to leave if the building is compromised.

clinic-room.description: A stripped-down guest room used for first aid, recovery, and quiet medical assessment. It is not a hospital and cannot replace professional treatment when injuries are serious.

back-office.description: The hotel's former administration office, now used for communications, records, supply checks, and limited contact with the faction dispatcher. Sensitive information is kept here only when necessary.

service-exit.description: A rear delivery entrance opening onto a narrow service lane. It is the safest route for discreet arrivals, supply movement, and departures when the front entrance is watched.

rooftop.description: A cluttered roof with water tanks, broken laundry lines, patched antennas, and a view toward Central Tokyo and Kurokawa. It serves as a lookout, meeting point, and emergency escape route.

The Velvet Lantern.basicInfo: A stylish casino and nightclub owned by Masato Vale, serving as a glamorous public venue and the Kurokawa underworld's discreet headquarters. Its gaming floors, bars, music, VIP rooms, and private negotiations conceal money laundering, coercive debts, powered enforcers, and restricted routes beneath the nightlife.
The Velvet Lantern.hiddenInfo: Masato Vale's public ownership and the club's legitimate entertainment operations provide cover for underworld finances and meetings. Its criminal role is known only to insiders, coerced staff, selected regulars, and people who have survived a private deal.

main-floor.description: A bright public casino and nightclub floor with music, gaming tables, slot machines, bars, cameras, and staff trained to notice unusual behavior. Ordinary patrons and Syndicate business overlap here.

main-entrance.description: A polished entrance with a velvet rope, discreet screening, valet access, and staff who remember regular patrons.

bar-lounge.description: A bar and lounge where patrons relax, deals begin casually, and rumors circulate beneath music and conversation.

vip-lounge.description: An exclusive lounge for wealthy guests, powerful associates, and private conversations. Access depends on invitation, money, reputation, or a useful secret.

security-office.description: A monitoring room with camera feeds, access logs, staff communications, and incident records. It can reveal movement, payments, and hidden relationships.

staff-corridor.description: A restricted hallway linking service rooms, staff entrances, storage, offices, and private floors. Employees use it constantly, making unauthorized movement risky but possible.

negotiation-suite.description: A sound-treated private room used for deals, debt settlements, recruitment, threats, and meetings between Syndicate representatives and outside parties.

counting-room.description: A secure financial room where cash, records, ledgers, and laundering arrangements are processed. It is valuable evidence and heavily protected when active.

service-entrance.description: A rear loading and staff entrance for deliveries, waste removal, private arrivals, and discreet movement of goods. It opens toward a narrow Kurokawa service route.

backstreet-route.description: A narrow route behind the club connecting delivery bays, fire escapes, and neighboring buildings. It is useful for surveillance, escape, smuggling, or an undercover approach.

hidden-exit.description: A concealed escape route through a maintenance passage and disused stairwell. It can bypass the lobby and lead toward rooftops or a secondary street.

Starbox Coffee.basicInfo: Busy student-friendly coffee shop where Minato works weekend shifts, with polished branding, café seating, takeout traffic, and a small back room for staff breaks and supplies.

cafe-floor.description: Bright café seating, display cases, outlets, and a counter where customers order drinks and pastries.

service-counter.description: Register, espresso machines, pastry display, and pickup shelf. Staff manage orders here during the morning rush.

kitchen.description: Compact preparation kitchen for drinks, syrups, pastries, cleaning supplies, and delivery orders.

window-seating.description: A popular row of seats overlooking the street, used by students, remote workers, and customers filming short Pulse clips.

staff-room.description: Small employee room with lockers, shift notes, supplies, and a place to take a short break away from customers.

Moonbucks Tea.basicInfo: Low-key tea shop with a quiet back room where Hyun works evening preparation and closing shifts.

tea-floor.description: Calm customer area with tea counters, low lighting, and small tables.

back-room.description: Staff preparation, inventory, and closing area.

Karaoke Kanari.basicInfo: Karaoke venue where Jinwoo works guest-hosting shifts with clear professional boundaries.

lobby.description: Reception, song-book displays, payment desk, and waiting benches.

karaoke-hall.description: Private rooms and shared corridors filled with music, requests, and rotating customers.

staff-room.description: Employee lockers, schedules, and break space.

Uniqloaf Clothing.basicInfo: Clothing shop with a fitting floor and alterations counter where students work retail and repair shifts.

sales-floor.description: Clothing racks, fitting rooms, displays, and customer service.

alterations-counter.description: Repair and tailoring station where Mika works under safety rules.

stockroom.description: Inventory, employee supplies, and shift storage.

WcDonalds.basicInfo: Late-opening fast-food restaurant with student-friendly shifts, counter service, a compact kitchen, and a staff area.

dining-floor.description: Counter seating, booths, order screens, and customer tables.

service-counter.description: Ordering and pickup counter with menu boards.

staff-room.description: Small break room and shift board.

Maidreamin Café.basicInfo: Themed café with scheduled service shifts, a performance-oriented customer floor, and staff preparation areas.

customer-floor.description: Themed tables, stage corner, and service aisles.

staff-room.description: Lockers, shift notes, and employee break space.

Konbini Castle.basicInfo: Convenience store with rotating student shifts, register service, stocked aisles, and a compact employee area.

sales-floor.description: Aisles, refrigerators, hot-food case, and customer checkout traffic.

register.description: Checkout counters, parcel service, and lottery display.

stockroom.description: Deliveries, inventory shelves, lockers, and staff supplies.

Maison Lumière.basicInfo: Elegant French bistro with candlelit tables, polished service, a curated menu, and a private dining room for formal meals or discreet conversations.

dining-room.description: Refined dining room with linen tables, soft lighting, and attentive service.

bar.description: Small wine and aperitif bar near the entrance.

private-room.description: Quiet reservation-only room for celebrations, negotiations, or confidential dinners.

Vesuvio Rosso.basicInfo: Lively Italian trattoria with family-style tables, red-checkered decor, generous portions, and a kitchen that treats every meal like a community event.

dining-room.description: Warm crowded dining room with shared tables, red-checkered cloths, and energetic conversation.

counter.description: Host stand, takeaway counter, and dessert display.

kitchen.description: Busy open kitchen with ovens, pasta preparation, and staff movement.

Seoul Ember.basicInfo: Korean barbecue restaurant with tabletop grills, private booths, shared side dishes, and smoky late-evening energy.

dining-floor.description: Tabletop grills, shared dishes, energetic groups, and staff who help manage the cooking.

private-booths.description: Semi-private grill booths suited to dates, celebrations, tense meetings, and group bonding.

service-counter.description: Reception, reservations, side-dish station, and payment counter.

kitchen.description: Prep kitchen and ingredient storage behind the grill service.

Kurogane Wagyu.basicInfo: High-end wagyu steakhouse with reservation-only seating, private booths, a visible chef counter, and an atmosphere of quiet expense.

dining-room.description: Elegant low-lit dining room with carefully spaced tables and premium service.

chef-counter.description: Counter seating overlooking the chef's preparation and grill work.

private-booths.description: Exclusive booths for business dinners, dates, family expectations, and discreet negotiations.

kitchen.description: Specialized grill kitchen, dry-aging storage, and controlled plating area.

Skyline Table.basicInfo: Rooftop restaurant with open-air seating, glass railings, Tokyo views, weather-sensitive service, and a small enclosed dining room.

rooftop-dining.description: Open-air tables overlooking Tokyo, with heaters, umbrellas, and a clear view of the changing skyline.

indoor-dining.description: Glass-walled dining room used during rain, strong wind, or colder evenings.

bar.description: Compact rooftop bar serving nonalcoholic drinks, cocktails, and evening specials.

kitchen.description: Service kitchen connected to the enclosed dining room and rooftop pass.

service-stair.description: Staff and emergency stair access connecting the rooftop restaurant to the building below.

Neon Reel Entertainment Complex.basicInfo: Large modern movie theater and arcade complex with multiple screening rooms, a bustling game floor, concessions, private event space, and late-night student traffic.

atrium.description: Main entrance atrium with ticket kiosks, posters, escalators, and paths to the theater and arcade wings.

cinema-lobby.description: Theater lobby with ticket counters, showtime boards, queues, and entrances to multiple screening rooms.

screening-halls.description: Cluster of standard movie theaters ranging from compact rooms to a large premiere auditorium.

arcade-floor.description: Bright arcade packed with rhythm games, claw machines, racing cabinets, fighting games, prize counters, and photo booths.

prize-counter.description: Redemption counter with plush toys, novelty prizes, and staff storage behind the display wall.

concessions.description: Large snack and drink counter serving popcorn, themed treats, and quick meals to cinema guests.

event-lounge.description: Reserved lounge for premieres, student celebrations, Pulse creator events, and private screenings.

staff-corridor.description: Restricted employee passage connecting theater operations, arcade supervision, and staff rooms.

service-kitchen.description: Back-of-house preparation area for concessions and event catering.

staff-room.description: Employee lockers, shift board, break tables, and security monitors.

Harajuku Prism Street.basicInfo: Colorful Harajuku-style fashion street lined with independent boutiques, vintage racks, accessory stalls, custom sneaker shops, beauty counters, and pop-up storefronts.

prism-crosswalk.description: Busy pedestrian crossing and street entrance surrounded by colorful signs, youth fashion, and Pulse-ready photo spots.

streetwear-row.description: Independent shops selling oversized silhouettes, graphic-inspired streetwear, layered outfits, and custom sneakers.

vintage-lane.description: Narrow lane of curated vintage clothing, thrift finds, handmade pieces, and rotating resale racks.

accessory-alley.description: Small boutiques for jewelry, bags, hair accessories, nail art, and colorful cosmetics.

sneaker-studio.description: Custom sneaker and shoe-painting shop with repair benches and appointment slots.

beauty-counter.description: Compact beauty and styling shop offering makeup, hair accessories, and quick student-friendly services.

pop-up-court.description: Open courtyard for weekend markets, limited drops, local designers, and creator events.

Azure Atelier Designer Row.basicInfo: Exclusive designer shopping street built around Azure Atelier, a luxury water-inspired fashion house whose tailored garments are favored by a certain water hero.

atelier-galleria.description: Elegant pedestrian lane of luxury storefronts, sculptural displays, and discreet security.

azure-atelier.description: Flagship boutique for Azure Atelier's ocean-inspired couture, performance fabrics, formalwear, and custom fittings.

private-fitting.description: Appointment-only fitting rooms where clients receive confidential measurements, alterations, and custom design consultations.

tideglass-jewelry.description: Luxury jewelry boutique specializing in blue glass, pearl, silver, and wave-shaped pieces.

mariner-tailoring.description: High-end tailoring house for precise suits, coats, formalwear, and discreet alterations.

gallery-café.description: Quiet designer café where clients, stylists, and visiting heroes can meet away from the main street.

service-corridor.description: Restricted back passage connecting deliveries, tailoring workrooms, and staff access.

Prism Gate Mall.basicInfo: Major all-purpose shopping complex connecting fashion, dining, entertainment, electronics, beauty, hobbies, daily necessities, and a rooftop public space.

main-atrium.description: Grand central atrium with information desks, seasonal displays, escalators, and direct access to the mall's major wings.

fashion-floor.description: Large fashion level with everyday clothing, accessories, youth brands, and a walkway toward Harajuku Prism Street.

designer-annex.description: Controlled-access luxury wing leading toward Azure Atelier Designer Row, with premium boutiques and private appointments.

beauty-floor.description: Cosmetics, salons, skincare, nail studios, and styling counters.

lifestyle-floor.description: Electronics, support-tech accessories, home goods, books, hobby shops, and collectibles.

food-hall.description: Busy food court and casual dining level with student seating, quick meals, desserts, and pop-up vendors.

entertainment-wing.description: Arcade annex, hobby venues, event space, and a connected entrance toward Neon Reel Entertainment Complex.

event-stage.description: Public event area for launches, seasonal festivals, Pulse livestreams, signings, and hero appearances.

underground-concourse.description: Underground passage with station access, convenience services, lockers, and late-hour foot traffic.

rooftop-deck.description: Open rooftop garden and observation deck overlooking the surrounding shopping district.

Sakura Lane Sharehouse.basicInfo: Furnished sharehouse in the Academy area offering eight individually assigned private bedrooms, shared facilities, and a safe rooftop terrace for residents to relax. It is an inexpensive, social residence for full-time workers, students, and other adult residents. Salina's group-house community can accommodate the incoming Class 6E residents here. It is not the player's Full-Timer home unless the player explicitly chooses or accepts a move there.

building-entrance.description: A welcoming entrance with mailboxes, package lockers, bicycle parking, and a noticeboard for house rules and resident announcements.

shared-lounge.description: Common lounge with sofas, dining tables, a television, and an open kitchen where housemates meet after work.

shared-kitchen.description: Communal kitchen with labeled storage, shared appliances, and enough counter space for casual meals or group cooking.

resident-hallway.description: Residential hallway leading to eight furnished private bedrooms and shared bathrooms, with stair access toward the rooftop.

garden-bedroom.description: A furnished private bedroom facing the planted courtyard, with a bed, desk, closet, and lockable door.

street-bedroom.description: A furnished private bedroom overlooking Sakura Lane, with a bed, desk, closet, and lockable door.

loft-bedroom.description: A bright upper-floor private bedroom with a bed, desk, closet, and lockable door, closest to the rooftop access.

courtyard-bedroom.description: A quiet furnished private bedroom near the courtyard side of the house, with a bed, desk, closet, and lockable door.

maple-bedroom.description: A furnished private bedroom with warm wood furnishings, a bed, desk, closet, and lockable door.

sunrise-bedroom.description: A furnished private bedroom with morning light, a bed, desk, closet, and lockable door.

lilac-bedroom.description: A furnished private bedroom with soft colors, a bed, desk, closet, and lockable door.

river-bedroom.description: A furnished private bedroom with a distant riverside view, a bed, desk, closet, and lockable door.

shared-bathroom.description: Clean shared bathroom facilities used by residents on the floor.

rooftop-chill-deck.description: A safe, ordinary rooftop terrace with permitted access, low railings, weatherproof chairs, potted plants, string lights, and views over Academy streets. Residents come here to cool off, talk, study, watch the evening sky, or have quiet time; it is not a combat arena or restricted hero facility.

laundry-room.description: Shared laundry room with coin-operated machines and a folding counter.

house-courtyard.description: Small outdoor courtyard with benches, bicycles, potted plants, and space for informal conversations.

Mizuno Heights.basicInfo: Older but maintained apartment building with affordable private studios and one-bedroom units. Thin walls and limited space are balanced by convenient access to ordinary neighborhood services.

building-entrance.description: Compact entrance with parcel lockers, mailboxes, intercoms, and a small management noticeboard.

residential-hallway.description: Narrow apartment corridor with doors to six private units and a shared utility closet.

unit-101.description: Private apartment Unit 101, a compact studio with a kitchenette, sleeping area, desk, bathroom, and limited storage.

unit-102.description: Private apartment Unit 102, a compact one-bedroom unit with a small dining table, kitchenette, bathroom, and practical storage.

unit-201.description: Private apartment Unit 201, a compact studio with a desk, books, kitchenette, sleeping area, and bathroom.

unit-202.description: Private apartment Unit 202, a compact one-bedroom home with a low sofa, kitchenette, sleeping area, bathroom, and practical storage.

unit-301.description: Private apartment Unit 301, a compact studio with plants, kitchenette, sleeping area, reading chair, bathroom, and limited storage.

unit-302.description: Private apartment Unit 302, a compact studio with a simple bed, work desk, kitchenette, bathroom, and organized storage.

stairwell.description: Narrow enclosed stairwell connecting the apartment floors to the rooftop.

rooftop.description: Quiet apartment rooftop with safety railing, utility equipment, water tank, and a view over residential Tokyo at sunset.

shared-laundry.description: Utility room with washing machines, dryers, and a folding surface for residents.

bicycle-shelter.description: Covered bicycle area beside the entrance, used by residents commuting to nearby shops and transit.

Lantern House Apartments.basicInfo: Renovated older apartment building in the Old Tokyo residential quarter, above workshops and small family businesses. Residents value courtesy, privacy, and neighborhood memory.

street-entrance.description: Lantern-lit entrance opening onto a narrow residential lane beside workshops and small shops.

residential-hallway.description: Renovated hallway combining modern fixtures with preserved wood details and quiet apartment doors.

private-apartment.description: Older renovated apartment with a compact kitchen, bathroom, living space, sleeping area, and views toward the surrounding historic streets.

shared-laundry.description: Small resident laundry room with practical machines and a window onto the service lane.

workshop-front.description: Public-facing row of ground-floor workshop doors and small business entrances where residents exchange greetings with local proprietors.

service-alley.description: Narrow maintained alley behind the building, used for deliveries, bins, and quiet access between neighboring properties.

Neon Gate Residences.basicInfo: Compact apartment building above a busy commercial strip of restaurants, karaoke, retail, and late-night businesses. It suits workers whose schedules run late.

commercial-lobby.description: Secure lobby with parcel lockers, mailboxes, elevator access, and the sounds of the businesses below.

residential-hallway.description: Compact upper-floor hallway leading to studio apartments and a shared utility area.

private-studio.description: Small studio apartment with kitchenette, bathroom, sleeping area, and sound-insulated windows facing the commercial street.

laundry-room.description: Shared laundry room used by residents working irregular or late shifts.

street-front.description: Busy covered sidewalk outside the building, with restaurants, karaoke entrances, retail shutters, taxis, and evening foot traffic.

Harborview Terrace.basicInfo: Comfortable mid-range apartment complex with balconies, shared facilities, and a longer commute to central jobs. Its residents enjoy calm waterfront surroundings and practical community amenities.

complex-entrance.description: Landscaped entrance with security access, mailboxes, parcel lockers, and a small management office.

residential-courtyard.description: Shared courtyard with benches, planted paths, and a clear view toward the waterfront district.

apartment-hallway.description: Clean residential hallway leading to private units and shared building facilities.

private-apartment.description: Comfortable studio or one-bedroom apartment with a balcony, kitchen, bathroom, living space, and more storage than the cheaper options.

private-balcony.description: Private balcony overlooking the neighborhood, useful for fresh air, quiet conversations, and watching evening lights.

shared-laundry.description: Resident laundry room with several machines and a folding counter.

bike-storage.description: Secure bicycle storage beside the entrance for residents commuting through the waterfront district.

waterfront-walk.description: Public walking path beside the residential complex, with benches and a route toward nearby shops and transit.

Harborlight Ferris Pier.basicInfo: A lively waterfront amusement pier with a large Ferris wheel, harbor views, ticket booths, casual food stalls, dessert counters, benches, and evening lights. It is a public leisure destination for dates, families, friends, tourists, and ordinary weekend outings.

pier-entrance.description: Waterfront entrance with ticket booths, maps, railings, public notices, and views toward the Ferris wheel.

ferris-wheel-plaza.description: Open plaza beneath the Ferris wheel with queue rails, benches, souvenir kiosks, and safe harbor views.

wheel-queue.description: Ordinary Ferris wheel boarding queue with shade structures, safety notices, staff gates, and numbered cabins beyond the loading platform.

food-stall-row.description: A row of casual waterfront food stalls selling takoyaki, grilled seafood, fries, crepes, soft-serve, drinks, and other affordable pier food.

harbor-dining-deck.description: Outdoor dining deck with ordinary tables, umbrellas, railings, harbor air, and places to eat food bought from the pier stalls.

waterfront-cafe.description: Small modern café serving coffee, tea, sandwiches, pastries, and seasonal harbor-themed desserts.

arcade-corner.description: Compact pier arcade with ordinary claw machines, rhythm games, photo booths, and a change counter.

Moonlit Scoops.basicInfo: A cheerful neighborhood ice cream shop with rotating seasonal flavors, soft-serve, sundaes, cones, cups, and a few sidewalk seats. It is a casual stop for friends, families, dates, and solo dessert runs.

shop-counter.description: Bright counter with flavor boards, free tasting spoons, toppings, cones, cups, and a small refrigerated display.

sidewalk-seating.description: A few ordinary outdoor tables and chairs where customers can eat ice cream and watch the street.

Crumb and Cloud.basicInfo: A cookie shop inspired by modern oversized-cookie bakeries, selling warm cookies, chilled milk, coffee, gift boxes, and rotating weekly flavors. The shop is popular for takeout, small celebrations, study breaks, and social-media photos.

order-counter.description: A compact counter displaying oversized cookies, flavor cards, milk, coffee, and boxed assortments.

window-bar.description: A narrow indoor window bar with stools for customers eating warm cookies and drinks.

Ringlet Donuts.basicInfo: A casual donut shop with glazed, filled, cake, and seasonal donuts, plus coffee and tea. It opens early for commuters and remains a friendly stop for students, workers, and late-afternoon snack runs.

display-counter.description: Front counter with trays of donuts, refrigerated drinks, coffee service, and a small menu board.

window-seating.description: Simple seating by the front windows for quick breakfasts, study breaks, and casual conversations.

Lantern Bowl Ramen.basicInfo: A grounded neighborhood ramen shop with counter seating, a few small tables, takeout service, and practical late-evening hours. It serves ramen, gyoza, rice bowls, water, tea, and rotating broth specials.

front-counter.description: Compact entrance and ordering area with a menu board, ticket machine, and visible counter seats.

ramen-counter.description: Open kitchen counter where staff prepare ramen, gyoza, and rice bowls in full view of customers.

small-tables.description: A few ordinary tables for small groups, quick meals, and quiet conversations.

Kurokawa Fresh Market.basicInfo: A compact neighborhood grocery store serving Kurokawa residents, apartment tenants, night workers, and small restaurants. It carries produce, packaged food, drinks, toiletries, household basics, and ready-to-eat meals.

entrance-checkouts.description: Automatic doors, baskets, checkout lanes, a small service desk, and shelves of discounted ready-to-eat meals near closing time.

grocery-aisles.description: Narrow aisles stocked with produce, packaged staples, snacks, drinks, toiletries, and practical household supplies.

冷蔵-section.description: Refrigerated cases with milk, bottled drinks, prepared meals, chilled noodles, desserts, and fresh ingredients.

Kurokawa Lantern Mart.basicInfo: A bright 24-hour convenience store on a busy Kurokawa nightlife street, selling snacks, drinks, hot counter food, toiletries, phone chargers, cigarettes, magazines, and basic daily necessities.

front-counter.description: Checkout counter with hot snacks, coffee machine, lottery terminal, tobacco cabinet, and parcel service desk.

aisles.description: Compact aisles of drinks, snacks, instant meals, toiletries, batteries, chargers, magazines, and umbrellas.

back-seating.description: A small indoor eating area with simple counter seats, a microwave, and a hot-water station.

Kurokawa Night Owl Konbini.basicInfo: A late-night convenience store near Kurokawa residences and side streets, used by shift workers, residents, performers, and people coming home after the nightlife district closes.

shop-floor.description: Ordinary convenience-store aisles with bottled drinks, snacks, instant noodles, toiletries, medicine cabinet items, and discounted bentos.

checkout.description: Small checkout area with a coffee machine, microwave, parcel pickup shelf, and a window toward the street.

Kurokawa Seven Corner.basicInfo: A 24-hour convenience store near the station approach, providing ordinary food, drinks, ATM access, parcel services, chargers, umbrellas, and quick meals for commuters and nightlife workers.

sales-floor.description: Bright aisles of packaged food, drinks, coffee, toiletries, stationery, batteries, and travel necessities.

registers.description: Checkout lanes with ATM, parcel counter, hot food case, and staff station.

eat-in-nook.description: Small counter seating by the window for quick meals and people-watching.

Kurokawa Ramen House.basicInfo: A modest late-night ramen shop serving noodles, gyoza, rice bowls, and simple drinks to residents, workers, and people leaving the Kurokawa entertainment district.

ticket-machine.description: Entrance with a ticket vending machine, menu photographs, condiment shelf, and a short waiting line.

counter-seats.description: Open kitchen counter with steaming ramen bowls, gyoza plates, and direct views of the cooks.

small-tables.description: A few compact tables for pairs and small groups seeking a quick late-night meal.

Kurokawa All-Night Diner.basicInfo: A 24-hour American-style diner on a Kurokawa side street, serving burgers, fries, pancakes, eggs, sandwiches, milkshakes, coffee, pie, and inexpensive comfort food for nightlife workers, residents, and people waiting out the night.

dining-room.description: Red-vinyl booths, chrome-edged tables, laminated menus, large street-facing windows, and a pie display under warm fluorescent lights.

counter.description: Long counter with swivel stools, coffee refills, condiment caddies, and a view of the open kitchen.

booths.description: Private booths for late-night meals, casual conversations, dates, studying, and tired workers.

kitchen.description: Open kitchen preparing burgers, fries, pancakes, waffles, eggs, bacon, grilled cheese, chicken sandwiches, milkshakes, coffee, pie, and rotating specials.

Kurokawa All-Night Donuts.basicInfo: A 24-hour donut shop near the nightlife district, serving fresh glazed, filled, cake, and seasonal donuts with coffee, tea, and simple takeout boxes for commuters, performers, and night-shift workers.

display-counter.description: Glass display filled with donuts, filled pastries, seasonal specials, and takeout boxes beside the register.

coffee-bar.description: Coffee and tea service with cream, sugar, microwaves, and a small prep counter for overnight staff.

window-seating.description: Simple window stools and narrow tables overlooking the neon street, useful for quick breakfasts and quiet late-night conversations.

Apartment 801.basicInfo: An empty Kurokawa apartment above a quiet side street, offering a private base for someone living outside respectable society. Floor-to-ceiling windows expose distant city lights and rain, while bare rooms contain almost nothing: a thin mattress, a small kitchenette, and an aching sense of isolation.
Apartment 801.hiddenInfo: The apartment's criminal associations, occupants, contacts, and stored information may be concealed, but the building and its areas are globally visible. Access can be restricted by keys, permission, reputation, or timing; never treat the location itself as hidden.

apartment-interior.description: A vast, nearly empty apartment interior with floor-to-ceiling windows, bare concrete, worn flooring, a thin mattress, and an unused kitchenette. Suitable for isolation, recovery, difficult conversations, meetings, and long-term schemes.

entry-stairwell.description: A narrow stairwell and apartment entrance opening onto a discreet Kurokawa side street. The building entry is visible, though access may be controlled by whoever currently occupies the apartment.

window-wall.description: Floor-to-ceiling windows and a low sill overlooking Kurokawa's lights and rain. A quiet place for late-night conversations, surveillance, reflection, and watching the neighborhood.

balcony.description: A narrow private balcony outside the apartment, overlooking Kurokawa's lights and rain. It is suited to quiet conversations, surveillance, smoking, cooling off, or watching the street below.

kitchenette.description: A nearly unused kitchenette with a sink, compact refrigerator, and limited counter space. It can support simple meals, evidence review, or tense conversations.

fire-escape.description: A visible fire escape outside the apartment windows, overlooking the side street and neighboring rooftops. It is not hidden, though access depends on safety and permission.

building-entry.description: The building's publicly visible entrance, with a buzzer panel, mailboxes, cracked tile, and a clear view toward the Kurokawa street. Visitors can wait here before access is granted or refused.

side-street.description: A visible Kurokawa side street beside the apartment building, with rain-slick pavement, shuttered storefronts, and passing pedestrians. Useful for meetings, deliveries, surveillance, and departures.

service-alley.description: A publicly visible service alley behind the building, used by deliveries, maintenance, and occasional neighborhood traffic. Atmospheric without being a secret location.
