rooftop.description: A shared rooftop with water tanks, safety rails, utility structures, and a broad view of Kurokawa. Ideal for late-night conversations, faction meetings, surveillance, and quiet decisions, subject to access and weather.

Midnight Shrine.basicInfo: A small, secluded shrine in Old Tokyo where late-night visitors come for quiet prayers and a moment away from the city.
Midnight Shrine.hiddenInfo: The shrine's boundary markers are stronger than they appear, but they are not an automatic defense against a yokai.

shrine-grounds.description: Stone steps, a modest offering box, and old lanterns beneath trees. The grounds are calm at first, but the surrounding darkness provides places for something supernatural to approach unseen.

lantern-approach.description: A narrow approach from the Old Tokyo street, marked by weathered lanterns and a torii gate. It offers a clear route away from the shrine during a dangerous encounter.

The Lair.basicInfo: An abandoned multi-room building informally nicknamed The Lair. Its eight unassigned bedrooms, kitchen, common room, meeting room, and rooftop make it a practical multiplayer headquarters that players can reclaim and shape.
The Lair.hiddenInfo: The Lair is stable enough to reclaim, but its utilities, security, and ownership history can become future organization story hooks.

bedroom-1.description: A small dusty bedroom with enough space for one player to establish a personal base. It remains unassigned until claimed in play.

bedroom-2.description: A small unassigned bedroom with a damaged wardrobe and a view of neighboring rooftops.

bedroom-3.description: A narrow unassigned bedroom with old shelves and a door that still locks.

bedroom-4.description: An unassigned bedroom with peeling paint, a ceiling light, and room for personal storage.

bedroom-5.description: A quiet unassigned bedroom at the end of the hall, with a cracked mirror and boarded window.

bedroom-6.description: An unassigned bedroom with a sturdy floor and a corner for equipment or work supplies.

bedroom-7.description: An unassigned bedroom with faded wallpaper and a view toward the street.

bedroom-8.description: The largest unassigned bedroom, suitable for a player who wants extra workspace.

kitchen.description: A neglected kitchen with a working sink, old counters, and limited appliances.

common-room.description: A broad room with mismatched chairs, worn couches, and open floor for planning or storage.

meeting-room.description: A former office with a long table, scarred chairs, dead wall screens, and privacy for organization meetings and speakerphone calls.

hallway.description: The central corridor connecting the bedrooms and shared rooms. It smells of dust, paint, and old rainwater.

rooftop.description: A rough rooftop with patched concrete, rusted railings, city views, and room for lookouts or future improvements.

Silver Screen Garden.basicInfo: Independent neighborhood cinema with art-house films, midnight screenings, small director talks, and a quiet rooftop garden for guests.

lobby.description: A compact cinema lobby with ticket windows, film posters, a small box office, and comfortable waiting benches.

screening-halls.description: Three intimate screening rooms for new releases, classic films, documentaries, and late-night features.

concessions.description: A modest counter serving popcorn, drinks, pastries, and specialty seasonal snacks.

rooftop-garden.description: A quiet rooftop seating area with planters and city views, open between screenings when weather permits.

Moonlight Multiplex.basicInfo: A large contemporary cinema with premium screens, immersive sound, family programming, fan events, and a busy late-evening crowd.

atrium.description: Bright entrance atrium with ticket kiosks, digital showtime boards, escalators, and a broad public meeting space.

cinema-lobby.description: Main theater lobby with ticket counters, queues, promotional displays, and entrances to the screening halls.

screening-halls.description: Multiple standard and premium auditoriums showing current releases, special events, and animated films.

concessions.description: Large snack counter serving popcorn, drinks, candy, hot food, and themed release promotions.

arcade-corner.description: Small entertainment area with claw machines, rhythm games, and photo booths near the theater exits.

event-stage.description: Flexible area for premieres, fan gatherings, school events, and cast or creator appearances.

Red Oven Pizza House.basicInfo: A casual neighborhood pizzeria known for blistered wood-fired pies, counter service, family tables, and generous takeout boxes.

dining-room.description: Warm dining room with family tables, red tile, open shelving, and a view toward the oven.

counter.description: Order counter with menu boards, pickup shelves, drinks, and takeaway boxes.

kitchen.description: Open kitchen centered on a wood-fired oven, dough preparation, toppings, and staff movement.

Night Slice Tokyo.basicInfo: A late-night pizza counter serving oversized slices, spicy toppings, garlic knots, and quick meals to students, workers, and nightlife crowds.

counter.description: Bright late-night counter with warming trays, slice displays, condiment bottles, and a few standing tables.

seating-area.description: Compact seating area with high stools, small tables, and a window overlooking the night street.

kitchen.description: Busy prep kitchen handling dough, ovens, toppings, delivery orders, and late-night rushes.

Amore al Forno.basicInfo: A romantic Italian pizzeria with handmade dough, seasonal toppings, candlelit tables, and a calm atmosphere suited to dates and celebrations.

dining-room.description: Softly lit dining room with intimate tables, ceramic plates, plants, and an open view of the baking ovens.

host-stand.description: Entrance and reservation desk with menus, waiting stools, and takeaway ordering.

oven-room.description: Visible preparation area with handmade dough, ingredient shelves, and stone ovens.

Champion's Pie Garage.basicInfo: A casual sports-themed pizza restaurant near the pier, with large pies, screens for live matches, communal tables, and a loud friendly atmosphere.

dining-room.description: Open dining room with communal tables, sports screens, booths, team colors, and a busy family-friendly crowd.

order-counter.description: Counter for whole pies, slices, drinks, and takeaway orders beside the open kitchen.

kitchen.description: Commercial kitchen with deck ovens, prep counters, refrigeration, and stacked pizza boxes.

game-corner.description: Small area with tabletop sports games and prize machines for waiting customers.

Redline Arms and Armor.basicInfo: A licensed firearms and protective-equipment retailer serving authorized civilians, security contractors, licensed heroes, and vetted professionals. Sales, storage, transfers, repairs, and training follow Japanese law and venue-specific access rules.
Redline Arms and Armor.hiddenInfo: The store does not sell weapons or ammunition casually. Access depends on identity, licensing, lawful purpose, age requirements, permits, training, inventory, and current legal restrictions. Students, vigilantes, criminals, and villains may be refused, reported, or offered only lawful protective or training alternatives. Never bypass legal safeguards or provide illegal acquisition routes. Armor may be available more broadly than firearms but remains subject to cost, fit, supply, and venue rules.

showroom.description: Supervised showroom displaying legally approved firearms, training equipment, protective clothing, helmets, body armor, and secure cases. No unsupervised handling.

service-counter.description: Staffed counter for identification checks, permits, paperwork, secure storage, transfers, repairs, and restricted-order questions.

fitting-room.description: Private fitting space for checking body armor, protective jackets, helmets, carriers, and mobility before purchase or authorized rental.

training-range.description: Restricted indoor range for approved customers and supervised instruction, with safety briefings, protective equipment, and controlled ammunition use.

range-office.description: Instructor and records office handling scheduling, licensing checks, safety documentation, and training plans.

secured-storage.description: Locked storage for regulated firearms, ammunition, armor orders, repairs, and items awaiting authorized transfer.

Bizarre Alley.basicInfo: A narrow service alley tucked behind older storefronts, lit by humming signs, vending-machine glow, and a single flickering security lamp. It is an ordinary public passage that becomes an absurd stage when Gogo and Deo turn their rivalry into a challenge.

alley-mouth.description: The brighter entrance beside a convenience store and side street, with pedestrian traffic and a clear route out.

service-run.description: The central stretch of the alley, wide enough for a tense standoff or short fight but cramped enough to create hazards.

back-lot.description: A dead-end loading space behind shuttered businesses, cluttered with bins, crates, and a locked utility gate.

Harborlight Beach.basicInfo: A public Tokyo Bay beach with broad sand, marked swimming areas, lifeguard stations, changing facilities, food kiosks, and a busy seasonal promenade. It supports ordinary recreation, beach sports, photography, casual work, and supervised water activities.

beach-entrance.description: Public entrance with signs, lockers, changing rooms, showers, rental counters, and access to the promenade.

main-sand.description: Broad maintained beach with marked swimming zones, umbrellas, volleyball space, towels, and open room for sunbathing or games.

lifeguard-station.description: Staffed elevated lifeguard post overlooking the marked swimming area, with rescue equipment and safety notices.

waterline.description: Supervised shoreline where visitors wade, swim in designated zones, look for shells, and watch the bay.

food-kiosk-row.description: Seasonal kiosks selling drinks, shaved ice, grilled snacks, sunscreen, towels, and inexpensive beach supplies.

promenade.description: Paved waterfront walk with benches, rental bikes, public art, and clear views toward nearby harbor attractions.

volleyball-court.description: Marked beach-sport area used for casual games, school outings, training, and public events.

Odaiba Shoreline.basicInfo: An urban waterfront beach and promenade beside Tokyo Bay, combining sand, seawalls, skyline views, public art, event space, and popular photo locations. It is a natural setting for dates, filming, modeling, social-media work, and public gatherings.

shoreline-plaza.description: Open waterfront plaza with event notices, public art, benches, and access to the sandy shoreline.

urban-beach.description: Maintained urban sand and shallow-water recreation zone with signs describing swimming and water-access rules.

waterfront-edge.description: Seawall and designated viewing edge overlooking the bay, with railings, lights, and strong skyline views.

skyline-promenade.description: Wide paved promenade used by walkers, cyclists, performers, photographers, and social-media creators.

photo-platform.description: Raised public viewing platform with a clear background for portraits, fashion shoots, livestreams, and sunset photography.

event-lawn.description: Flexible public lawn for pop-up markets, seasonal festivals, fitness sessions, and small sponsored events.

Saltglass Kitchen.basicInfo: A bright seaside restaurant on Harborlight Beach serving grilled fish, noodles, rice bowls, and seasonal dishes with bay views.

dining-room.description: Open dining room with broad windows, beach-facing tables, a counter, and ordinary restaurant seating.

beach-patio.description: Outdoor patio with umbrellas, windbreaks, and views over the sand and water.

Undertow Bar.basicInfo: A relaxed waterfront bar beside Harborlight Beach with mocktails, cocktails, live music, and sunset seating. Evening access follows venue rules.

bar-room.description: Casual bar interior with a service counter, small tables, music equipment, and windows toward the bay.

sunset-deck.description: Outdoor deck with railings, low tables, and direct views of the shoreline at dusk.

Sea-Salt Soft Serve.basicInfo: A small beach ice cream shop specializing in sea-salt soft serve, chilled desserts, fruit toppings, and takeout cones.

service-counter.description: Bright counter with soft-serve machines, menu boards, toppings, and a short queue area.

beach-window.description: Takeout window opening toward the promenade, with standing tables and views of the beach.

Salt Sprinkle Bar.basicInfo: A dedicated sea-salt ice cream bar offering experimental flavors, tasting flights, and a counter facing Harborlight Beach.

tasting-counter.description: Long tasting counter with rotating sea-salt flavors, sample spoons, and a view toward the water.

flavor-lab.description: Small preparation space where staff develop seasonal combinations and limited-edition desserts.

Tide-Table Dining.basicInfo: A casual beach restaurant with picnic-style tables, seafood sandwiches, vegetarian plates, and family-friendly daytime service.

main-dining.description: Casual dining room with durable tables, open windows, and quick daytime service.

picnic-terrace.description: Outdoor terrace with shared tables, shade umbrellas, and a clear view of the sand.

Moonpool Lounge.basicInfo: A quieter night-oriented lounge near Harborlight Beach offering drinks, small plates, and sheltered seating away from the busiest sand.

lounge-floor.description: Low-lit lounge with comfortable seating, a small service bar, and muted coastal decor.

covered-deck.description: Sheltered deck with curtains, heaters, and a quieter view toward the water.

Boardwalk Bites.basicInfo: A compact counter-service beach eatery selling fried seafood, shaved ice, quick meals, and snacks for visitors on the move.

service-counter.description: Fast counter-service window with menu boards, pickup shelves, and beach-facing standing tables.

prep-kitchen.description: Compact commercial kitchen handling snacks, drinks, and quick meals.

Dock One.basicInfo: A public recreational dock at Harborlight Beach with railings, benches, small-boat access, fishing notices, and open bay views.

dockhead.description: Main dock platform with benches, railings, safety equipment, and views across the bay.

launch-gate.description: Controlled shore-side access point for supervised small-boat launches and dock events.

Dock Two.basicInfo: A second waterfront dock near Harborlight Beach used for evening views, supervised launches, event access, and harbor photography.

viewing-dock.description: Long waterfront platform with lights, benches, railings, and space for harbor photography.

access-ramp.description: Accessible ramp connecting the dock to the public waterfront walk.

The Alcove.basicInfo: A secluded venue beneath a concrete bridge, set apart from Harborlight Beach and reached by a side route from the waterfront. It has sheltered tables, muted lights, and an intimate atmosphere.

under-bridge-seating.description: Sheltered seating beneath the bridge with concrete pillars, muted lights, weather protection, and a distant view of the beach.

side-approach.description: A narrow but public approach from the waterfront, separated from the main beach by the bridge structure and service fencing.

Ryota's Yacht.basicInfo: A sleek private yacht used by successful pro hero Ryota for travel, charity appearances, hero networking, private recovery, and carefully controlled media events. It is anchored off the Chikara waterfront and is not automatically open to the public.

boarding-dock.description: A secured boarding point with access checks, mooring lines, life jackets, and a clear view of the beach and city skyline.

main-deck.description: Polished open deck with seating, shaded tables, rescue equipment, and room for supervised gatherings or formal receptions.

salon.description: Comfortable interior salon used for meetings, meals, interviews, and private conversations away from the open water.

hero-briefing-room.description: Compact meeting room with navigation displays, emergency plans, communications equipment, and space for professional hero discussions.

upper-observation-deck.description: Raised observation deck with uninterrupted views of the bay and city, used for quiet reflection, photography, and private conversations.

Primes Headquarters.basicInfo: A secure residential hero headquarters where all five Primes members live, train, coordinate deployments, receive visitors, and recover between missions. The building combines a public-facing operations center with private residential floors, medical support, tactical rooms, communications infrastructure, and shared spaces designed to make the team function as a household as well as an emergency-response unit.
Primes Headquarters.hiddenInfo: The building's public floors are carefully managed for branding, while the residential floor has informal rules and private tensions that management does not fully understand. A sealed service route connects the medical wing to an emergency evacuation point. Mika knows the surveillance blind spots; Aoi knows which emergency supplies are missing; Haruto knows which construction decisions were expensive; Ryota knows which doors teammates avoid.

interview-room.description: A controlled broadcast studio inside Primes Headquarters with two interview chairs, a small production desk, microphones, softbox lights, cameras, acoustic panels, monitors, and discreet Primes branding. The room is designed for polished introductions, sponsored interviews, and carefully managed public statements.

front-lobby.description: A polished public lobby with a Primes emblem, reception desk, security screening, visitor seating, display cases, and carefully controlled sightlines for media appearances.

operations-floor.description: The team's command level, containing briefing rooms, mission planning tables, secure communications stations, sponsor liaison offices, and Ryota's leadership workspace.

communications-suite.description: Mika's communications hub, filled with monitored screens, dispatch equipment, signal shielding, drone cradles, and emergency coordination systems.

training-floor.description: A modular combat and rescue training space with reinforced surfaces, collapsible obstacles, medical observation equipment, and adjustable environmental hazards.

medical-wing.description: A compact professional treatment area with examination rooms, recovery beds, trauma supplies, and equipment for post-mission monitoring. Aoi frequently argues with staff here about discharge times.

rec-room.description: A dedicated recreation room where the Primes can decompress away from cameras and mission schedules. It has a home theater, sectional seating, full-size pool table, board-game shelves, snack and drink bar, arcade cabinet, and warm lounge lighting. The room is one of the few spaces designed for them to be ordinary young adults rather than public heroes.

shared-lounge.description: The residential common room with couches, entertainment systems, a balcony, and enough visible evidence of five very different people living together. The connected shared kitchen is the practical center of daily life.

shared-kitchen.description: The shared kitchen used by all five Primes members: a large island, refrigerator covered with schedules and sponsor magnets, mismatched mugs, pantry shelves, a commercial range, and a dining table where arguments, late meals, and rare honest conversations happen away from cameras.

residential-floor.description: A secure private floor containing six bedrooms, bathrooms, laundry facilities, a quiet study, and a residential corridor. Five rooms belong to the Primes members; the sixth is reserved for a player, guest, or future team member.

bedroom-ryota.description: Ryota's orderly private bedroom: understated furniture, training equipment, mission files, a few personal keepsakes, and blackout curtains for the rare nights he manages to sleep.

bedroom-emi.description: Emi's practical bedroom with combat gear, recovery supplies, discarded sponsor packages, athletic clothing, and a television usually playing something louder than necessary.

bedroom-mika.description: Mika's colorful bedroom and content-planning space with clothing racks, product samples, ring lights, charging stations, campaign boards, and several phones within reach.

bedroom-haruto.description: Haruto's refined bedroom with quiet luxury furnishings, carefully arranged books, a private wardrobe, family gifts he has not discarded, and a view chosen for privacy rather than prestige.

bedroom-aoi.description: Aoi's functional bedroom with rescue boots by the door, medical textbooks, laundry waiting to be folded, emergency bags, practical furniture, and a chair that is frequently used for exhausted naps.

bedroom-six.description: A flexible private bedroom reserved for the player, a guest, or a future Primes-affiliated resident. It contains a bed, desk, wardrobe, secure storage, and a blank wall awaiting personalization.

Kurokawa Legal Office.basicInfo: A respected independent law office in a mixed-use Kurokawa building, with a reception desk, two consultation rooms, a compact records room, and a private office for attorney Ken Kuroda. It is known for careful, unusually capable representation in cases involving powered incidents, superhero crimes, superhuman legal disputes, collateral damage, unlawful use of abilities, and vigilante cases, while still serving ordinary clients who need practical representation.
Kurokawa Legal Office.hiddenInfo: Ken's reputation has grown through difficult cases where ordinary legal assumptions fail: proving responsibility after powered collateral damage, challenging excessive force, protecting civilians caught between heroes and villains, negotiating restitution, defending vigilantes whose actions require careful factual scrutiny, and separating public panic from admissible evidence. The office does not excuse violence or guarantee acquittals. It insists on lawful process, informed consent, confidentiality, evidence preservation, and client-specific strategy. Superpowered clients may seek help here, but representation is never automatic and conflicts of interest must be addressed before a case begins.

reception.description: Small public reception area with a waiting bench, intake desk, legal notices, and a printer.

consultation-room.description: Private client room with a table, chairs, accessible layout, and secure space for confidential conversations.

hallway.description: Short interior hallway connecting reception, consultation rooms, records, and Ken's office.

records-room.description: Locked records room with filing cabinets, case folders, and controlled document storage.

ken-office.description: Ken Kuroda's private office with a desk, legal texts, accessible organization tools, a cane stand, and a window overlooking Kurokawa's streets.

The Iron Labyrinth.basicInfo: A dense graveyard of rusted shipping containers stacked stories high, forming a claustrophobic maze of steel. Scavengers and smugglers from the Nightshade Exchange use the interior hollows as temporary stashes and ambush points. The air smells of salt and oxidation, and the shifting stacks often groan under their own weight.

Sovereign Refinery.basicInfo: A massive, derelict petrochemical refinery characterized by its towering, jagged pipes and leaking storage vats. It serves as a primary hideout for high-risk criminals and those fleeing Metropolitan Police jurisdiction. Toxic puddles and flammable gas pockets make combat here extremely hazardous for those without environmental protection.

Neon Sluice Canal Lights.basicInfo: A concrete-lined waterway filled with sluggish, multi-colored runoff that never freezes. Bridges made of scrap metal connect the two banks, where desperate residents and 'Blacklisted' runaways set up makeshift camps. It is a known site for illegal power-testing and disposal of incriminating evidence by the Kurokawa Underworld.

Vault-7 Sorting Hub走向.basicInfo: A partially operational automated sorting facility that has been repurposed by the Obsidian Crown Agency as a secure meeting point. The machinery often jerks to life without warning, creating a dangerous environment of moving conveyor belts and crushing hydraulic presses. Heavy security patrols the perimeter to keep curious Chikara students away.

Orizuru Grid-Prime.basicInfo: A high-tension substation surrounded by humming transformers and crackling electrical arcs. The ground is scorched, and the air crackles with static, attracting individuals with electrical or magnetic powers. It is a frequent site for violent territory disputes between rival gangs seeking to siphon off unregulated power.

The Proving Flat.basicInfo: A vast, cratered concrete lot where heavy machinery was once tested, now used for illicit 'no-holds-barred' matches. Unlicensed combatants and power-users gather under the glare of portable floodlights to settle debts through brute force. The Metropolitan Police rarely intervene here due to the high density of hostile powered threats.

The Hollow Hull.basicInfo: The rusted hull of an ancient cargo ship that ran aground in a shallow silt-filled bay. It serves as a neutral-ground black market where information brokers and fixers trade stolen academy secrets and experimental hero gear. The interior is a vertical warren of damp cabins and echoing engine rooms.

Redline Tenements.basicInfo: A cluster of leaning, abandoned worker apartment blocks being reclaimed by aggressive vines and weeds. Misfit Hero Agency members often come here on low-pay search-and-rescue missions to find missing persons hiding in the crumbling ruins. The structural instability of the buildings makes every floor a potential pitfall trap.

Summit Bazaar.basicInfo: A sprawling rooftop market and transit hub perched atop the central Tower Five. Vendors sell street food, recycled electronics, and black-market hero memorabilia under wind-beaten awnings. The area is a neutral ground for information exchange and a common starting point for vertical expeditions.

Core-Link Engine Room激.basicInfo: A heavily fortified sub-basement complex that houses the regional heating and power systems. Local technicians and roughnecks manage the aging machinery, often clashing with saboteurs from the Nightshade Exchange looking to hold the towers' utilities for ransom. The air is thick with steam and the rhythmic thumping of industrial pistons.

Aether Gardens.basicInfo: A collection of hanging garden terraces and solar panel arrays located on the windward side of the towers. It is a quiet, green space frequented by retirees and student trainees looking for a place to practice aerial maneuvers. The Metropolitan Police maintain a small kiosk here to monitor the sky-lanes for unauthorized flyers.

Mid-Level Junction.basicInfo: An abandoned high-speed transit station halfway up Tower Three that has been converted into a training ground. Vigilantes and aspiring heroes use the empty tracks and rusted train cars to practice close-quarters combat. The lack of surveillance makes it a prime spot for the Obsidian Crown Agency to scout for potential recruits.

The Iron Tangle.basicInfo: A hazardous exterior construction zone where a bridge between Tower Eight and Nine collapsed years ago. The area is a graveyard of dangling steel beams and high-tension cables, now inhabited by scavengers and 'Gutter-Divers' who specialize in retrieving items dropped from the upper levels. It is notoriously dangerous due to high winds and unstable footing.

Unit 402 Clinic.basicInfo: A small, independent medical clinic tucked away in a converted three-bedroom apartment. Dr. Arisaka provides off-the-books treatment for powered injuries, making it a frequent stop for Blacklisted individuals who cannot risk a public hospital. The clinic is always crowded with patients waiting on mismatched folding chairs.

The Chute Basins.basicInfo: The main waste disposal and recycling facility at the base of the towers. Massive trash chutes from all levels converge here into sorting pits. It is a foul-smelling, hostile territory controlled by local gangs who sift through the city's refuse for discarded tech and sensitive corporate data.

The Vein Pathways激.basicInfo: A cluster of narrow service corridors and maintenance shafts that bypass the main elevators. It is the primary route for the Kurokawa Underworld to move contraband through the district without detection. The walls are covered in shifting graffiti that serves as a coded map for those who know how to read it.

Tetsu Iron Palm Gym.basicInfo: Tetsu Iron Palm Gym: converted storefront and former dojo between the Academy and Kobuncho; neutral ground under an unwritten truce with the Shirogane crew, the Daigo syndicate and the Honebi Collective. Tetsu (retired Shirogane enforcer, prosthetic left leg) and regulars Kaito Serizawa, Riko Amane, Sayaka Mizuhara, Genta Oda, Masaru Hachiya. Scene of the Thursday rematch and the doorstep beating (3b-3).
Tetsu Iron Palm Gym.hiddenInfo: The gym is run by Tetsu-san, a retired enforcer who once fought for the Shirogane crew before going straight, and his regulars Kaito Serizawa, Riko Amane, Sayaka Mizuhara, Genta Oda, and Masaru. The building was originally a dojo founded decades ago, and its walls still carry faded calligraphy from the old master who taught here before the ward's gangs carved up the territory. Tetsu-san keeps the gym neutral ground under an unwritten truce with the Shirogane crew, Daigo syndicate, and Honebi Collective, but Renji Kuroba's crew has been testing that truce by recruiting local youths and pressuring the gym's younger members. The recent brawl with the Joestar brothers has drawn dangerous notoriety to the gym, and Tetsu-san worries the footage review tonight could bring academy or gang attention down on his regulars.

Front Entrance & Reception.description: A converted storefront with a wide glass front, a worn sign reading 'TETSU IRON PALM GYM' in faded kanji, and a small reception desk where visitors sign in. A short hallway leads past a heavy bag rack toward the main training floor.

Main Training Floor.description: The main open training space with worn canvas mats, heavy bags, a freestanding dummy, and a wall of mirrors. Regulars drill striking and footwork here under Tetsu-san's watchful eye.

Tea Corner & Office.description: A low-ceilinged corner with a battered tea table, mismatched stools, and a small electric kettle. Tetsu-san holds court here, and the gym's regulars gather to talk shop and neighborhood news.

Private Storage Room.description: A narrow converted storage room, four paces wide and six long, with a single blue training mat, bare drywall, and a bolted freestanding dummy. A short shelf holds rolled hand wraps and a cracked timer.

Back Alley Exit.description: A cramped back door opening onto a trash-lined alley behind the gym. A rusted fire escape climbs the wall, and the alley connects to the wider Kurokawa Ward streets.

Kobuncho.basicInfo:
Kobuncho is a nightlife district whose daytime quiet hides a web of cabaret hostesses, retired yakuza fixers, off-duty hero informants, and the staff of its many snack bars and izakayas. The district was once a thriving entertainment quarter, but a decade of gentrification pressure and a string of unsolved disappearances of host club workers have left its residents wary and tight-lipped. The Shirogane crew, Daigo syndicate, and Honebi Collective all quietly claim pieces of the district's protection rackets, and their rivalry keeps the streets tense even in daylight. A recent string of late-night muggings near Shutter Alley has residents blaming the crews, though some whisper the real culprit is something that moves through the district's unmarked tunnels.

Canon hierarchy (user-decided post-t326): Region > Location > Area. Club Lumiere, Tetsu Iron Palm Gym and the licensing annex (Ward Licensing Services) are AREAS of Kobuncho, not separate locations; Shutter Alley is a real Kobuncho area (the engine places the party there); The House, the old bathhouse, Holding Pens and Maintenance Sub-Level are also Kobuncho areas. Kurokawa is the syndicate, not a district.

Neon Lantern Street.description: The narrow main drag of Kobuncho, lined with tightly packed two- and three-story buildings plastered in layered posters for cabaret clubs, snack bars, host clubs, and izakayas. Daytime staff haul crates of bottles and ice through half-raised shutters while a few regulars smoke under sun-bleached awnings.

Club Lumiere.description: A pink-cursive cabaret club with a laminated lunch-set menu taped to its glass door, its sequined-jacketed hostess sweeping the front step. Inside, a dim lounge of velvet booths and a small stage sits quiet until evening.

Shutter Alley.description: A cramped back lane behind the main street where delivery trucks idle and workers stack crates of canned beer onto hand carts. Shuttered warehouse doors and unmarked stairwells hide storage rooms and a few unofficial gambling dens.

Kobuncho Station Front.description: A small preserved station at the district's edge with a cracked wooden sign, its platform serving the local line. A few commuters and day-trippers pass through, and a cramped kiosk sells cigarettes, magazines, and warm canned coffee.

The Stale Tap.description: A weathered izakaya with a sun-bleached awning where older men in rumpled suits smoke and talk in low voices. Inside, a long counter serves grilled skewers and cheap beer, and the back room hosts a private table favored by local fixers.

Maintenance Sub-Level.description: A narrow, damp passage beneath the annex, smelling of stagnant water and old copper. The walls are lined with thick, vibrating power cables that hum with a low, unsettling frequency.

The House.description: A sprawling, tiered underground amphitheater lit by harsh crimson floodlights and ringing with the roars of a desperate crowd. A blood-stained sand pit sits at the center, surrounded by reinforced steel cages and Kurokawa guards.

Holding Pens.description: A series of cramped, lightless iron cells where 'indebted' fighters are kept in chains between matches. The air is thick with the scent of antiseptic and fear, guarded by a heavy-duty mechanical lock system.

humming room.description: Visited, sparsely described in the engine. Connects to humming room.

Club Kagerō.description: Club Kagero ('heat haze', Neon Lantern Street): publicly shuttered satellite club; in truth an invite-only after-hours front with a 'school' on the closed upper floor. Collapsed into the earth at t327 (Peach Aftershock) with its archive.

Kobuncho.director_note: Club Lumière, Tetsu Iron Palm Gym and Ward Licensing Services are separate Voyage locations (Neon Lantern Street paths lead to them); the annex here is the street-level area.

Club Lumière.basicInfo: Club Lumiere (Neon Lantern Street): the Joestar crew's OWNED, fortified base, jointly owned by Jovian and Jostin (Speedwagon Foundation transfer via Aurelia Voss). Half-repaired pink-cursive cabaret with Foundation-standard security, rear connection to Shutter Alley. Staff: Maki Hayashida (manager, records), Natsumi Arai, Chiho Moriyama, Tomoe, Kaede Shishido (debts unresolved), Airi. Hostesses: Airi Kurosawa, Mirei Tachibana, Noa Amemiya, Rika Saotome, Sena Amagawa. Nobu and Hana keep gear caches here. "Safehouse" means Club Lumiere until a real one exists. A pink-cursive cabaret club with a laminated lunch-set menu taped to its glass door, its sequined-jacketed hostess sweeping the front step. Inside, a dim lounge of velvet booths and a small stage sits quiet until evening.
Club Lumière.hiddenInfo: Club Lumière is a half-repaired cabaret in Kobuncho's Neon Lantern Street, run by hostesses Maki Hayashida, Natsumi Arai, Chiho Moriyama, Tomoe, and Kaede Shishido, now newly owned by the Joestar brothers under a Speedwagon Foundation transfer. The venue was damaged in a brawl and is being rebuilt with Foundation-standard security, but its old debts and Kaede's personal obligations remain unresolved. A teenage crew has been shaking down local shops near the canal, and the club's back door access and routes are held by Gara in Shutter Alley, who demands the stolen protection money and the organizer's name in return. The hostesses and crew are wary of Kurokawa sniffing around the ward, and the club's legal identity is still fragile while repairs and paperwork settle.

Main Lounge.description: The main lounge and bar floor, freshly repaired with a gleaming new security door, warm light spilling from behind frosted glass. Booths line the walls, a stage sits at the far end, and the bar counter is clear and polished.

Back Office.description: A bright, renovated operations room with a whiteboard on one wall, gear bags lined along the other, and red-and-black Joestar-patched jackets hanging ready. This is where the crew briefs, stores equipment, and plans operations.

Kitchen.description: A compact working kitchen where Maki prepares the house curry and gourmet meals, with prep counters, a large stove, and a small pantry stocked for late-night service.

Stage Alcove.description: A raised performance platform with a small soundboard and lighting rig, currently half-repaired and draped with drop cloths. Hostesses and crew gather here between sets and briefings.

Storage Closet.description: A narrow, windowless room off the kitchen holding spare chairs, cleaning supplies, and the construction debris awaiting removal. A locked cabinet here stores the club's old ledgers and unregistered records.

Tidegate Market.basicInfo: The heart of the ward, a raised market district of fish stalls, noodle shops, and repair yards built on timber pilings above the tidal flats. Traders, boat crews, and residents gather here for goods, news, and work, while licensed heroes keep a visible patrol presence along the main boardwalk. The market is the only reliable dry crossing between the ward's flooded halves.

Sluicework Station.basicInfo: A decommissioned flood barrier and pumping station that now serves as a neutral meeting ground for waterfront crews, fixers, and anyone who needs to talk without being overheard. The old control room still works, and the station's operators sell passage, storage, and information to whoever pays. Its catwalks and machinery galleries are a common site for quiet deals and tense standoffs.

The Drowned Quarter.basicInfo: A flooded residential district that the recent storm surge reopened, its lower floors now underwater and its rooftops connected by improvised rope bridges and plank walkways. Scavengers dive the submerged shops and homes for salvage, while squatters and smugglers use the drowned streets as a hidden route. The water is cold, murky, and full of hazards, and the district floods and drains with the tide.

Keelwright Yard.basicInfo: A working boatyard and dry dock where crews repair fishing boats, ferries, and the occasional smuggler's hull without asking questions. The yard is loud with welding, hammering, and the smell of diesel and paint. Its foreman keeps a ledger of who owes what, and the yard doubles as a hiring hall for waterfront labor and less legal work.

Tankfield Peninsula.basicInfo: A cluster of rusted storage tanks and abandoned fuel depots on a low peninsula, now used as a staging ground for contraband transfers and a refuge for crews that want to stay out of sight. The tanks echo with footsteps and dripping water, and the ground is slick with old fuel residue. Patrols avoid the area after dark, and the peninsula's only road is easily watched.

Kobune Bluff Shrine.basicInfo: A small shrine and teahouse on a raised bluff that survived the flooding, tended by an elderly woman who remembers the ward before the sea took it. The shrine is a quiet refuge where residents leave offerings and seek blessings for safe voyages. The teahouse serves as a place to hear old stories and current rumors, and the proprietor keeps watch over the drowned district below.

The Old Seawall.basicInfo: A long, crumbling seawall that marks the old boundary of the ward, now a popular walking route and a contested line between the market's patrols and the crews who work the outer waters. The wall is lined with faded murals and memorial plaques for those lost to past storms. At night, the wall becomes a meeting point for deals and a lookout for approaching boats.

The Grounded Freighter.basicInfo: A half-sunken cargo terminal where a container ship ran aground years ago and was never fully removed. The tilted decks and stacked containers form a maze of corridors, holds, and makeshift shelters. Scavengers, squatters, and smugglers share the wreck, and its flooded lower holds are rumored to hide things best left undisturbed. The ship groans and shifts with the tide.

Ward Licensing Services.basicInfo: Ward Licensing Services, a municipal front for Kurokawa’s Legitimacy branch. Connects to Maintenance Sub-Level and Neon Lantern Street.
Ward Licensing Services.hiddenInfo: Ward Licensing Services is a municipal front for Kurokawa's Legitimacy branch, where the captain launders official permits and licensing records to shield syndicate operations. Old Man Koga, a retired enforcer turned gatekeeper, grants access to the captain's seat only to those who prove themselves in the underground circuit. The stooped clerk, Sonobe, has quietly kept duplicate ledgers of every falsified document for years, waiting for someone worth handing them to. The captain is currently expecting a delivery of compromised licensing files that would expose eleven officials, and a masked vigilante has been watching the building for the same evidence.

ground-floor.description: Ward Licensing Services, a municipal front for Kurokawa’s Legitimacy branch. Connects to Maintenance Sub-Level and Neon Lantern Street.

Front Office.description: A cramped front office where a stooped man in glasses sorts folders behind a cluttered desk, a kettle whimpering on a hotplate. A hand-lettered sign and a grimy window face the street, with a narrow back hall leading deeper into the building.

Back Hall.description: A dim corridor lined with peeling municipal notices and a single buzzing bulb, its second door opening to the captain's seat. A service ramp at the far end connects to the alley and the underground circuit.

Paper Vault.description: A windowless records room packed floor-to-ceiling with steel shelving of licensing files, permits, and faded ledgers. A single desk holds a terminal and a stack of folders marked with red tabs.

Captain's Seat.description: A cramped office where the Legitimacy captain works behind a heavy desk, walls covered in framed licenses and a corkboard of names. A locked filing cabinet and a shuttered window face the alley.

Service Ramp.description: A narrow concrete ramp leading down to the service corridor and the underground circuit, lined with stacked crates and a shuttered print shop. A masked vigilante's van is parked at the alley mouth.

Roof Access.description: A tar-papered rooftop with a rusted water tank and a fire escape, offering a clear view of the alley and the shuttered print shop below. A loose grate hides a drop into the captain's office.

Goshiki High-Rises.basicInfo: Chiikawa Park is a rare patch of green squeezed between Tower Four and Tower Five, built on the site of an old community center that was demolished during the housing project's early years. The park is maintained by a rotating group of elderly residents and a retired gardener named Oba-chan, who tends the flower beds and keeps the mascot statue's paint from flaking entirely. Beneath the playground's rubber matting, a sealed storm drain leads to an abandoned maintenance tunnel that smugglers from the Nightshade Exchange occasionally use to move goods between towers. The park's food stalls are run by a loose cooperative of vendors, some of whom quietly pass information to the Metropolitan Police kiosk in exchange for protection from the local crews. A few of the tower's shut-ins have taken to leaving notes and small offerings at the mascot statue, treating it as a neighborhood shrine of sorts.

Chiikawa Park.description: A small green pocket at the base of two towers, with playground equipment, benches, and a chipped mascot statue of the round white character. Food stalls strung with paper lanterns line the edges, and an old vendor flips takoyaki at a corner cart while local kids chase each other around the swings.

Lantern Food Stalls.description: A row of food carts and stalls under wind-beaten awnings, where vendors sell takoyaki, grilled skewers, and sweet taiyaki. Paper lanterns hang unlit overhead, waiting to be switched on for the evening rush.

Sky-Bridge Plaza.description: A concrete plaza where the park meets the base of the towers, marked by a rusted sky-bridge overhead and a cluster of benches. Tower residents pass through on their way to the elevators, and a few watch the park from the balconies above.

Tower Five Lobby.description: The ground-floor entrance hall of Tower Five, with a bank of high-speed elevators, a small convenience kiosk, and a notice board covered in flyers. A security guard sits at a desk near the turnstiles, keeping an eye on the comings and goings.

Maintenance Scaffold Stairwell.description: A narrow, rusting exterior stairwell and freight lift shaft that climbs the outside of the towers, used by maintenance crews and smugglers alike. The metal grates rattle underfoot, and the wind howls through the gaps between floors.
